action: Issues the physical/e-job card with photo to the household
note: job card valid 5 years; entitles up to 100 days work/year

action: Final approval, sanctions the ration card, allots the category and Fair Price Shop
on_reject: rejection with recorded reasons; appeal to DGRO
note: card-issuing authority sitting in the district collectorate

action: Prints the ration card, seeds Aadhaar, links the FPS, delivers / enables digital download
note: issuance and FPS assignment via URCMS/e-PDS

action: NFSA grievance: the District Grievance Redressal Officer hears appeals on rejection or delay
on_reject: further appeal to the State Food Commission (NFSA s.16)
note: NFSA s.14 grievance channel; DGRO role often held by a district officer

action: Checks form completeness and documents, forwards the file to the Supply Inspector of the area
on_reject: returns incomplete form for correction
note: preliminary document check and routing

action: Identify the two demographic updates needed: name (new/hyphenated surname) and address (marital home).
note: Name and address are separate demographic-update requests but can be lodged in one visit. Applicant self-service step; not a listed UP-revenue post.

action: Signs/issues the official allotment order directing the private school to admit the allotted child
on_reject: school refusal escalated to BSA/CEO
note: binding order under s.12(1)(c); school cannot charge fees

action: Parent reports to the allotted school within the deadline for final document verification
time_limit: within the reporting window on the allotment order
on_reject: non-reporting forfeits the seat; complaint to BEO/BSA
note: reporting step is by the parent at the allotted private school

action: Citizen submits mutation application with registered deed/succession papers at the Tehsil counter
on_reject: Application not accepted if documents incomplete; resubmit with corrections
note: Report of transfer is made to the Tehsildar under s.34

action: Registers/diarises the application, assigns a case number and issues a dated receipt
note: Diarising starts the statutory clock for disposal

action: Opens the mutation file, verifies fee, and routes it to the field revenue staff
note: File prepared for field enquiry

action: Enter the conversion in the revenue record; update mutation to reflect residential/non-agricultural land.
note: Land use must be actually used within one year or the permission may be withdrawn.

action: Verifies residence/income/land records in rural areas, corroborates the SI report
on_reject: discrepancy noted in report
note: revenue-side field verification (rural cases)

action: Countersigns/validates the revenue verification and income-residence certification
on_reject: returns for re-verification
note: revenue authority attesting eligibility inputs

action: Scrutinises eligibility against NFSA priority-household / AAY exclusion criteria
on_reject: recommends rejection with reasons
note: eligibility scrutiny before forwarding to the sanctioning officer

action: Approves eligible applications at sub-division level within delegated authority
on_reject: rejection recorded with reasons
note: sanctioning authority where power is delegated to SDM/tehsil level

action: Digitally sign the certificate; make it downloadable from the e-District portal.
note: UP domicile certificate is lifetime-valid. Some states/certificate types require renewal (state-specific, uncertain).

action: Download digitally signed certificate from portal using tracking number; verify QR/authentication.
note: Offline alternative: collect from Tehsil / Jan Seva Kendra counter.

action: On delay past the statutory limit or wrongful rejection, hear the first appeal and direct issuance.
on_reject: Second appeal to the District Magistrate / designated senior appellate authority; grievance via CM Helpline (1076) / IGRS.
note: First Appellate Authority under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 / Uttarakhand Sewa Ka Adhikar Adhiniyam, 2011. A wrongful rejection can ultimately be challenged before the Collector or by writ petition (rarely needed).

action: Confirm the trade needs a corporation licence and its category; identify required extra clearances.
note: At the Nagar Nigam trade-licence / health section or Nagrik Suvidha Kendra. Fee slab and clearances (fire/health/pollution) depend on trade category.

action: Assemble ID/address proof, premises proof + owner NOC, property-tax/holding number, category NOCs.
note: Category NOCs may include Fire NOC, FSSAI food licence, UPPCB consent for polluting trades. Exact checklist varies by corporation.

action: File the trade-licence application online with documents and prescribed fee; get application number.
note: Via UP e-Nagar Sewa portal (e-nagarsewaup.gov.in) or the corporation office / Nagrik Suvidha Kendra counter. Intake only.

post_name: Licence Inspector (real designation; corporation licence/tax inspector)
action: Scrutinise the file and record any objection or demand for additional documents.
on_reject: Applicant cures objections / resubmits.
note: Post is a corporation-specific designation outside the standard list (Licence/Tax Inspector under the trade-licence or health section).

action: Inspect premises to confirm trade matches declaration and meets health/safety norms.
on_reject: Adverse report returned to applicant with reasons.
note: For dangerous & offensive / food & health trades, the corporation health wing (CMO office / MO / sanitary inspector) inspects under the 1959 Act licensing provisions.

post_name: Licence Superintendent / Zonal Officer (real designation; corporation delegated officer)
action: Recommend grant or rejection on the inspection and scrutiny reports.
on_reject: Recommendation of rejection escalates to sanctioning officer for order.
note: Delegated recommending officer varies by corporation (Zonal/Additional/Deputy Commissioner or Licence Superintendent). Designation outside standard list.

action: Gather supporting documents from the UIDAI Regulations Schedule for name (PoI) and address (PoA).
note: Name: marriage certificate or gazette notification or other accepted PoI in new name. Address: PoA in new name, OR Head-of-Family (HoF) proof + Proof of Relationship. Acceptable-document list is Schedule to the Aadhaar (Enrolment and Update) Regulations, 2016 — verify current list.

action: Choose channel: myAadhaar online portal (address only) or Aadhaar Seva Kendra in person (name + address).
note: Online supports address update only and requires a registered mobile for OTP. Name update generally requires a centre visit. Name may be updated at most twice on ordinary documents; further changes need gazette notification.

action: Book appointment or walk in at an Aadhaar Seva Kendra / enrolment centre for in-person update.
note: Centres are UIDAI-run or registrar-operated (often hosted at post offices/banks). Appointment booking available online where offered.

action: Fill Aadhaar Update Form with corrected name and address; capture applicant's biometrics.
note: Operator uses Update Client Standard/Lite. Post is a UIDAI-registered enrolment-agency operator, not a listed UP-revenue post (task is run by UIDAI, a central authority).

action: Verify submitted documents against UIDAI Schedule; scan originals; collect the update fee.
on_reject: Operator refuses if documents insufficient; applicant re-lodges with correct PoI/PoA, or escalates via 1947 if wrongly refused.
note: Demographic-update fee is a fixed UIDAI charge (Rs 50 per update per official charge schedule; Rs 75 is also cited — verify current amount). Online and in-person fees may differ.

action: Issue acknowledgement carrying the Update Request Number (URN) or Enrolment ID (EID).
note: In-person: 14-digit URN/EID on receipt. Online: Service Request Number (SRN) sent by SMS. Keep it — it is how status is tracked.

action: Review the request and documents; validate the demographic change against records.
time_limit: 30 days (90% of requests); up to 90 days outer bound
note: Central UIDAI back-end processing. Online-uploaded documents are verified at this stage rather than at the counter. Post is a UIDAI central function, outside the listed UP-revenue posts.

action: Gather residence, identity, age proofs and self-declaration affidavit; confirm state's residence-duration threshold.
note: UP typically requires proof of at least ~3 years' residence; exact document set and residence-duration rule are state-specific (uncertain).

post_name: Applicant (Citizen) / Common Service Centre (Jan Seva Kendra) operator
action: Submit application online via state e-District portal or a Jan Seva Kendra; pay statutory fee.
note: UP: edistrict.up.gov.in / e-Sathi (esathi.up.gov.in); Uttarakhand: edistrict.uk.gov.in. Fee ~Rs.15 in UP. An acknowledgement / tracking number is issued.

action: Scrutinise application and attachments for completeness; forward down to field revenue officer for verification.
on_reject: Application returned to applicant for correction/resubmission via the same portal.
note: Tehsil counter / e-district back-office triage before field verification.

action: Verify applicant actually resides at stated address for the required period; conduct field/neighbourhood check.
on_reject: Adverse verification report can lead to rejection; applicant may re-apply with stronger residence proof.
note: Village/ward-level revenue officer (Lekhpal in UP/Uttarakhand). Normally the longest, most variable stage.

action: Review the Lekhpal's field report, countersign/endorse, and forward up to the Tehsildar.
note: Kanungo / Revenue Inspector is the supervisory revenue tier between Lekhpal and Tehsildar.

action: Review verified report and approve issuance of the Nivas Praman Patra.
on_reject: Rejection order stated with reason; appeal to First Appellate Authority (SDM) under the Janhit Guarantee / Sewa Ka Adhikar Act.
note: Tehsildar is the designated issuing authority for UP/Uttarakhand domicile certificates (acting under the DM/Collectorate). Time limit runs under the state service-guarantee act.

action: Separately apply for building-map (naksha) sanction from the panchayat/development authority before starting construction.
on_reject: Building sanction refusal follows the local body / development-authority appeal route, distinct from the revenue appeal.
note: Distinct second track: the Section 143 order only reclassifies land use; a building/naksha sanction is a separate approval. Unauthorised construction risks fine/demolition.

action: Check eligibility: search family by mobile/Aadhaar/ration/family-ID on portal or Ayushman app.
on_reject: If not found in UP list, apply for state add-on / check 70+ Vay Vandana; in Uttarakhand all permanent residents qualify under AAUY.
note: PMJAY eligibility differs by state: UP uses SECC-2011 + state-added lists via SACHIS; Uttarakhand's AAUY is UNIVERSAL for all permanent residents regardless of income. Everyone aged 70+ is eligible nationwide under Ayushman Vay Vandana.

action: Gather Aadhaar of member being enrolled, registered mobile, ration/family-ID; Uttarakhand: residence proof.
note: Aadhaar of the person being enrolled is mandatory for eKYC. Exact accepted document list is set by the State Health Agency and can vary; confirm at the enrollment point.

post_name: Village Level Entrepreneur (VLE) - Common Service Centre / or self via Ayushman App
action: Go to a CSC, empanelled-hospital Arogya Mitra desk, or self-initiate on the Ayushman app.
on_reject: If CSC/VLE refuses or blocks, escalate to the CSC District Manager.
note: Enrollment points: CSC/VLE, Arogya Mitra kiosk at an empanelled hospital, designated government facility (PHC/CHC/district), or self-service via the Ayushman app (BIS 2.0) which still routes to an operator/auto-approver.

action: Operator searches family in beneficiary database and initiates eKYC for the member.
on_reject: If member not traceable, escalate to District Implementation Unit under the CMO/State Health Agency.
note: Arogya Mitra / Ayushman Mitra is the official PMJAY frontline enrolment-and-facilitation post at hospitals and camps.

action: Run Aadhaar eKYC (biometric/OTP or face auth), capture live photo, submit for approval.
on_reject: eKYC failure (Aadhaar mismatch): correct Aadhaar demographics at Aadhaar centre, then retry.
note: Under BIS 2.0, eKYC uses Aadhaar OTP/biometric/face authentication plus live photo; each family member is enrolled individually so eKYC repeats per member.

action: Consider the application and police submission and decide whether to order FIR registration and investigation
on_reject: Criminal revision, or writ under Article 226 / s.528 BNSS (High Court inherent power)
note: This is the decisive step of the escalation: under s.175(3) the Magistrate must now also weigh the police's explanation for refusal before directing investigation. An order here compels the station to register the FIR and investigate.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC) — private complaint bench
action: As an alternative, file a private complaint; Magistrate examines complainant on oath and may take cognizance directly
on_reject: Dismissal is appealable/revisable; can be pursued alongside the s.175(3) route
note: s.223 BNSS (successor to s.200 CrPC): the Magistrate examines the complainant and witnesses on oath and may take cognizance directly, bypassing the police entirely. New proviso to s.223(1): the proposed accused must be given an opportunity of being heard before cognizance. Distinct from the s.175(3) direct-to-police route.

post_name: Director General of Police (DGP) office / UP Police online grievance portal (UPCOP / e-FIR cell)
action: In parallel, lodge an online/e-FIR or written grievance for eligible offence types
on_reject: Portal non-action feeds the Janhit Guarantee appeal (step 5) and the SP complaint (step 4)
note: s.173(1) BNSS recognises information by electronic communication, valid once signed within 3 days. UP Police run online reporting (UPCOP/e-FIR) but scope is generally limited offence types (e.g. vehicle/property theft, cyber crime), not all serious bodily offences — verify offence-eligibility on uppolice.gov.in. A parallel channel, not a substitute for the s.173(4)/s.175(3) chain.

action: Where refusal involves a rights violation or police misconduct, file a separate complaint of police inaction
on_reject: Independent forum; does not compel FIR registration but records misconduct
note: A real but adjunct route for police inaction implicating rights; it addresses misconduct rather than compelling registration, which remains the function of s.175(3). Use alongside, not instead of, the core chain.

action: Receive and register complaint; assign it to the jurisdictional Food Safety Officer for action.
on_reject: Escalate to Commissioner of Food Safety, Uttar Pradesh (FSDA HQ).
note: DO heads district food-safety administration under the state Commissioner of Food Safety; the district-health office the citizen resolves to.

action: Inspect the shop/restaurant premises and verify the complaint on the ground.
note: FSO is the frontline enforcement officer under Section 38, FSS Act, 2006.

action: Lift a food sample under prescribed procedure; divide into parts and seal per Section 47.
note: Sampling and division of sample under Sections 41-47, FSS Act and Rule 2.4, FSS Rules, 2011; one part sent to Food Analyst.

post_name: Food Analyst, notified food laboratory (FSDA lab)
action: Analyse the sample and issue a report on whether food is substandard, misbranded, or unsafe.
on_reject: Analyst informs DO and Commissioner with reasons if 14-day window cannot be met.
note: Rule 2.4 (FSS Rules 2011): analysis within 14 days. Allahabad HC (Kewal Dairy v. State of UP, 2024) treats analyst-report date as the date of offence.

action: Review Food Analyst report; decide whether to adjudicate, prosecute, or drop.
on_reject: FBO/complainant may seek re-analysis by referral to the Central Food Laboratory under Section 46.
note: DO decides the enforcement route on the analyst report; sanction/consent to prosecute rests with DO under the FSS Act.

action: Adjudicate lesser offences (substandard, misbranded) and impose monetary penalty.
on_reject: Appeal to the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal under Section 70, FSS Act.
note: Adjudication of penalties under Section 68, FSS Act, 2006; Adjudicating Officer is of ADM rank (state-notified).

action: Try serious offences (unsafe food, injurious adulteration) on prosecution filed by the DO.
on_reject: Appeal to the High Court per the criminal-appeal procedure.
note: Serious offences under Sections 48-59 tried by Special Court under Section 69/section on special courts; prosecution requires DO consent.

post_name: Commissioner of Food Safety, Uttar Pradesh (FSDA)
action: On inaction, escalate; Commissioner supervises DO/FSO and may direct action or transfer.
on_reject: Further escalation to FSSAI central grievance mechanism; District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission for compensation; RTI on action taken.
note: Commissioner of Food Safety is the state head under Section 30, FSS Act; parallel consumer-forum and RTI routes available.

action: Print the submitted form and hand the signed hard copy plus documents to the institution
note: Physical submission to the college is required; the online form alone does not advance the application.

action: Conducts field enquiry, checks khatauni/khasra entries and possession, files field report
on_reject: Adverse field report may lead to rejection or conversion to contested case
note: first person a citizen meets for any land matter

action: Verifies and countersigns the Lekhpal's field report and khatauni check for correctness
on_reject: Report returned to Lekhpal for correction
note: Kanungo supervisory layer over the Lekhpal

action: Reviews field verification, ensures record consistency, forwards case to the Tehsil court
note: supervisory layer over the field staff

action: Issues proclamation (public notice) inviting objections from interested parties
note: s.35 proclamation; objections define uncontested vs contested branch

action: Lists the case for hearing before the Tehsildar/Naib Tehsildar after the objection period lapses
note: Reader manages the revenue court cause-list

action: Hears uncontested cases and passes the mutation order directing khatauni amendment
time_limit: target disposal within 45 days of application
on_reject: Appeal to Sub-Divisional Officer (SDM) within 30 days of the order
note: s.35(1) uncontested branch: NT directs amendment

action: For contested cases, adjudicates the dispute after hearing parties and passes the mutation order
on_reject: Appeal to SDM within 30 days; further to Collector/Commissioner
note: s.35(1) contested branch decided by Tehsildar; may take longer

action: Gives effect to the order by amending the khatauni (record of rights) entry
note: Record update executed at village level

action: Updates and preserves the amended record of rights in the tehsil record room
note: maintains the authoritative record copy

action: Issues a certified copy of the updated khatauni to the applicant
note: Certified copy is proof of mutation

action: Citizen applies via e-District/CSC or Tehsil counter; application captured with documents
on_reject: Incomplete applications returned for correction
note: e-District UP is the official channel

action: Generates the acknowledgement number and dated receipt, starting the service clock
note: Acknowledgement triggers the Janhit Guarantee time limit

action: Conducts field verification of residence/caste/income at the declared address and files report
on_reject: Negative verification can lead to rejection
note: Lekhpal checks khatauni, voter list, neighbours

action: Cross-checks and endorses the Lekhpal's verification report
on_reject: Report returned for re-verification
note: supervisory endorsement of field report

action: Verifies the report against records and forwards the file to the signing authority
note: record-check layer

action: Places the verified file before the Tehsildar/SDM for signature
note: Reader manages the signing queue

action: Reviews and digitally signs the caste/income/domicile certificate (SDM where designated)
time_limit: within the Janhit Guarantee statutory limit (~7-15 working days total)
on_reject: Appeal to First Appellate Officer within 30 days; second appeal within 60 days
note: designated officer under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011

action: Delivers the digitally-signed certificate via e-District download / CSC to the applicant
note: Certificate verifiable online by certificate number

action: Publishes RTE round notification and readies the state RTE portal, block school list and seat matrix
note: admission is only into entry class (Class 1 / pre-primary) per s.12(1)(c)

action: Parent applies online on the state RTE portal, uploading eligibility documents and choosing neighbourhood schools
note: citizen-facing step; submission is by the parent online

action: Receives application plus documents and verifies eligibility (age, EWS/DG income/caste, residence, distance)
on_reject: reapply in next round or appeal to Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA)
note: neighbourhood: within 1 km (primary) / 3 km (upper primary)

action: Confirms the verified applicant pool for the block/district and forwards the eligible list into the lottery
on_reject: grievance to BSA / District Education Officer
note: only BEO-verified applications enter the draw

action: Oversees the online lottery/random allotment of verified children to specific schools per seat availability
on_reject: waitlist / subsequent round; appeal to CEO/BSA
note: lottery is the decisive allotment event under the 25% quota

action: Allotted private school admits the child free of charge and records enrolment against the RTE seat
on_reject: school denial appealable to BSA / District Education Officer
note: actual admitting authority is the private school head

action: Confirms admission, records the child for state reimbursement, and closes the grievance channel
on_reject: appeal escalates BEO -> BSA -> District Education Officer
note: state reimburses per-child cost to the school under s.12(2)

action: Household submits registration application for a job card at the Gram Panchayat with ID/photos
note: registration is free; no fee may be charged

action: Verifies household details, residence and adult members claiming registration
on_reject: complaint to Gram Panchayat / Block Development Officer
note: verification done in the village for transparency

action: Gram Panchayat approves registration and orders issue of the job card to the household
on_reject: appeal to Programme Officer / Block Development Officer
note: job card issued in presence of local residents

action: Receives the worker's dated written work application and issues a dated acknowledgement receipt
on_reject: can also apply to the Programme Officer at block if the GP refuses the receipt
note: dated receipt is the legal trigger for the 15-day guarantee under s.3

action: Prepares/selects a work estimate from the shelf of projects to be opened for the demanded labour
note: work drawn from the approved GP shelf of projects

action: Sanctions the work and directs allotment of employment to the applicant household
time_limit: work must be allotted within 15 days of application
on_reject: failure triggers unemployment allowance under s.3(1); grievance to Programme Officer/Ombudsperson
note: the 15-day guarantee is the core statutory entitlement

action: Opens the muster roll and records daily attendance of workers at the worksite
on_reject: discrepancy raised at social audit / to Programme Officer
note: attendance read out to workers at day's end for transparency

action: Measures completed work in the Measurement Book to determine task-rate wages
on_reject: remeasurement / grievance to Programme Officer
note: wages proportional to JE measurement against task norms

action: Checks measurement, prepares the wage/muster-roll bill and forwards the Fund Transfer Order for payment
note: electronic FTO routes wages to worker accounts

action: Authorises wage payment; wages credited to workers' accounts
on_reject: delay compensation at 0.05% per day of unpaid wage under s.3(3)
note: delay beyond 15 days triggers automatic compensation

action: Gram Sabha conducts social audit of works, muster rolls and payments
on_reject: findings referred to Ombudsperson / Programme Officer for redress
note: social audit is the primary statutory accountability route

action: Receives the citizen's building plan and documents online/at counter, generates acknowledgement receipt
note: OBPAS single-window intake; registration of application

action: Checks completeness of documents and fee, forwards the file to the technical branch
on_reject: deficiency memo to applicant for resubmission
note: preliminary completeness check

action: Conducts site inspection, measures plot, verifies setbacks and ground reality against the plan
on_reject: adverse site report returns file for correction
note: field measurement and site-report to higher engineers

action: Technical scrutiny of the plan against bye-laws, FAR, coverage, setbacks; endorses the JE report
on_reject: raises query/objection to applicant via OBPAS
note: AutoDCR auto-scrutiny supplemented by AE bye-law check

action: Reviews AE scrutiny, confirms structural/FAR compliance, recommends the file upward
on_reject: returns file with objections
note: engineering-side recommendation before planning vetting

post_name: Building / Town Planning Officer (Nagar Niyojan Adhikari)
action: Vets the plan for zoning, land-use, master-plan and planning-norm conformity
on_reject: planning objection returned to applicant
note: town-planning vetting

action: Final technical clearance for large/high-value projects exceeding delegated limits
on_reject: returns with technical objection
note: only for cases above lower officers' delegated FAR/area limit

action: Sanctions plans within the delegated financial/area limit on the Commissioner's behalf
on_reject: rejection with recorded reasons
note: delegated sanctioning authority for routine/mid-size plans

action: Grants final sanction for plans beyond the delegated limit; approves the permit
on_reject: rejection with recorded reasons; appeal within 30 days
note: head sanctioning authority (or Vice-Chairman in a development authority)

action: Issues the stamped sanction letter / permit and sanctioned drawings via OBPAS
on_reject: deemed-approval if not communicated within statutory time; appeal within 30 days of rejection
note: deemed-approval provision under Ease of Doing Business

action: Citizen submits application and documents; clerk registers and issues acknowledgement receipt
note: intake at Supply Office / e-district / CSC counter

action: Conducts field/home verification of the family, residence and eligibility details
on_reject: adverse verification report can lead to rejection
note: primary NFSA field verification; visits the applicant's home

action: Approve or reject the update; on approval, commit the corrected name/address to the Aadhaar record.
on_reject: Rejection reason is stated; applicant resubmits with stronger documents, then escalates via 1947 / UIDAI grievance portal / regional office if unresolved.
note: This is the decisive step that grants the request. UIDAI is the central statutory authority under s.54 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016.

action: Track status by URN/SRN and download the updated e-Aadhaar PDF once approved.
note: Status at myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in Check Aadhaar Update Status. Fresh e-Aadhaar can be downloaded and printed once the change reflects.

action: Escalate stalled, wrongly-rejected, or refused requests via 1947, help@uidai.gov.in, or the grievance portal.
on_reject: Further escalation to the regional UIDAI office; ultimately RTI or writ remedy.
note: If processing exceeds ~90 days, call 1947 or email help@uidai.gov.in. Regional UIDAI office is the next tier. Grievance mechanism under UIDAI, not a district/municipal office.

action: Confirm plot is rural farmland outside municipal/development-authority limits so Section 143 revenue route applies.
on_reject: If plot falls inside MDDA/municipal or master-plan area, apply to that development authority instead.
note: Jurisdiction is location-specific. A 2020 Cabinet move routed some conversions to development authorities within their areas; for rural khasra the SDM/Section 143 route via landuse.uk.gov.in remains the live path.

action: Obtain current khatauni, khasra and najri naksha (site sketch) confirming land is classified agricultural and unencumbered.
on_reject: Clear pending mutation, tenancy or encumbrance disputes before applying.
note: Records pulled from the tehsil / Bhulekh; needed as application enclosures.

action: Submit Section 143 application on landuse.uk.gov.in with documents; pay Rs.1,000 non-refundable scrutiny fee.
on_reject: Incomplete documents returned for correction at intake.
note: Tehsil-office clerk receives and checks document completeness. Docs: ID/address proof, photo, khatauni, khasra, land photo, najri naksha, declaration form.

action: Verify application and enclosures, issue receipt, and forward the case to the Tehsildar.
time_limit: 2 days (forward to Tehsildar; receipt within 7 days if filed by post)
note: SDM / Assistant Collector is the deciding authority under Section 143.

action: Review SDM referral and order a field report from the Revenue Inspector/Lekhpal within ten days.
note: Case routed down the revenue chain for ground verification.

action: Inspect plot; report on boundaries, access, ownership, disputes, government/canal/forest claims and public interest.
on_reject: Adverse ground report (canal-command, forest/ESZ, dispute) can lead to rejection.
note: Revenue Inspector / Lekhpal field visit — the step where timelines most often slip.

action: Review the field report and submit it with remarks back up to the SDM.
Issue public objection notice inviting objections to the proposed land-use change.
on_reject: Sustained objections trigger a hearing and may defeat the application.
note: Mandatory statutory objection period; the main reason the real timeline exceeds the SOP's headline figure.

action: Hear any objections, then require payment of conversion charge (3% of circle-rate value) via challan.
on_reject: Conversion charge is refundable if application is rejected at verification stage.
note: Conversion charge = 3% of circle rate; scrutiny fee (Rs.1,000) already paid and non-refundable.

action: Pass the Section 143 declaration/order reclassifying the plot to non-agricultural (residential) use.
on_reject: Appeal to the District Magistrate/Collector within 30 days; further revision to Divisional Commissioner / Board of Revenue.
note: This is the decisive approval. Grounds for rejection: forest/ESZ, encumbrance, dispute, incomplete docs.

post_name: BIS 2.0 System / State Health Agency Verifier (SACHIS in UP; SHA in Uttarakhand)
action: System auto-approves exact matches above threshold; below-threshold records route to SHA verifier.
on_reject: Rejected/stuck record: escalate to the State Health Agency (SACHIS / Atal Ayushman SHA) grievance cell or District Implementation Unit under the CMO.
note: This is the decisive step. BIS 2.0 auto-approves high-confidence matches instantly; ambiguous ones go to a manual SHA verifier. No statutory SLA — turnaround ranges same-day to several days.

post_name: Self / Beneficiary or VLE / Arogya Mitra
action: Once approved, download or print the Ayushman card from app / bis.pmjay.gov.in self-print.
note: Card downloadable via Ayushman app, beneficiary portal, or self-print at bis.pmjay.gov.in. Card carries family cover up to Rs 5 lakh/year (amount/scope may differ under converged state schemes).

post_name: Ayushman Mitra (Arogya Mitra) at empanelled hospital
action: At admission, present card; Arogya Mitra raises pre-authorization to insurer/SHA/TPA for cashless care.
on_reject: If asked to pay at an empanelled hospital for a covered package, that is itself a grievance — escalate to hospital grievance nodal officer / helpline 14555.
note: Cashless ONLY at empanelled hospitals and ONLY for listed procedure packages; OPD and non-listed items generally excluded. Verify empanelment and package coverage before admission.

post_name: National Helpline 14555 / State Health Agency Grievance Cell / CMO District Implementation Unit
action: Escalate eligibility, enrolment, rejection, or treatment-refusal grievances.
note: National helpline 14555 (also 1800-111-565) for eligibility/enrolment/grievance. Rejected records -> SHA (SACHIS in UP; AAUY-SHA in Uttarakhand) grievance cell or CMO-led District Implementation Unit. Treatment-time refusal -> hospital grievance nodal officer.

action: Report institutional birth (Form 1) to local Registrar within 21 days; give baby's name if chosen.
note: For a home birth the parent/head of household is the informant and reports directly. Institutional births are reported by the hospital under s.8 RBD Act.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Registrar's desk, Nagar Nigam)
action: Receive the birth report at the Nagar Nigam registration desk; enter details into the CRS portal.
note: In a municipal-corporation area the Registrar of Births & Deaths function sits with the Nagar Nigam. Filing is via crsorgi.gov.in; UP uses e-District (edistrict.up.gov.in), Uttarakhand uses Apuni Sarkar / e-Services. Parents' + informant's Aadhaar now mandatory (2023 amendment).

post_name: Registrar of Births & Deaths (Nagar Nigam) — designated officer under the Chief Medical Officer (CMO)
action: Verify particulars and supporting proof against the reported record.
on_reject: Re-submit with corrected particulars; appeal under s.25 to the District Registrar.
note: The Registrar is designated by the state under s.7 RBD Act; in Nagar Nigam areas commonly under the CMO / municipal health wing. Exact desk/officer title varies by corporation.

action: If reported within 21 days, register the birth on the normal record — no penalty.
on_reject: Appeal under s.25 RBD Act to the District Registrar.
note: s.13(1): registration within 21 days is free/routine. This is the normal-path approval that decides the request.

action: Delayed 21-30 days: register on written requisition and payment of prescribed late fee.
on_reject: Appeal under s.25 to the District Registrar.
note: s.13(1) as amended (2023). Late fee typically nominal (approx. Rs 2-25 by state rules). This tier applies only if step 4 was missed.

action: Delayed 30 days-1 year: grant written permission after affidavit; then Registrar registers on late fee.
on_reject: Appeal under s.25 to the District Registrar; or move to the post-1-year magistrate-order route (step 7).
note: s.13(2): registration in this window needs written permission of the prescribed authority (state rules commonly designate the SDM / Executive Magistrate or a Registration officer) plus affidavit and late fee.

action: After 1 year: register only on the order of a magistrate after verification, with affidavit and fee.
on_reject: Appeal the order; or s.25 RBD appeal to District Registrar.
note: s.13(3) as amended (2023) replaced the earlier court-order requirement with an order of the District Magistrate / authorised Executive Magistrate (states may delegate to SDM/Tehsildar). Verification uses hospital, immunization or school records.

action: Register the birth on the CRS record following the approval tier reached.
note: Registration is completed and signed off in CRS once the applicable approval (steps 4-7) is in hand.

action: Issue the official digital birth certificate (Form 6); first copy free/nominal.
time_limit: state RTS limit (commonly 7 days; UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam)
on_reject: Service-delivery appeal under the state right-to-services law; s.25 RBD appeal.
note: Under the 2023 amendment the CRS digital certificate is the single nationally-accepted document. Downloadable from CRS / e-District (UP) / Apuni Sarkar (Uttarakhand); CSC / Jan Seva Kendra are facilitation counters.

action: Optional: add or correct the child's name to the register within the state-defined window.
time_limit: state rule window (commonly up to 1 year, sometimes extendable)
note: s.14 RBD Act: name can be added later if the child was unnamed at registration. Later corrections fall under s.15.

action: If Registrar delays or refuses, appeal the action/order within 30 days.
time_limit: appeal within 30 days; decided within 90 days (s.25)
on_reject: Further escalate to the Chief Registrar (state Directorate of Economics & Statistics / Health).
note: s.25 (inserted by 2023 amendment) creates a statutory appeal to the District Registrar, to be decided within 90 days. The District Registrar supervises registration in the district.

post_name: Chief Registrar of Births & Deaths (state Directorate of Economics & Statistics / Health)
action: Final supervisory escalation for non-issuance across the state registration system.
on_reject: Grievance under the state public-services-guarantee mechanism (UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam / Uttarakhand RTS); or writ.
note: The Chief Registrar is the state-level superintending authority under s.4 RBD Act.

post_name: Medical Officer in Charge (Hospital / Nursing Home)
action: Institution where birth occurred reports the event to the Registrar and gives parents the birth-report/discharge slip.
on_reject: If institution fails to report, the informant (parent/head of household) files the reporting form directly under s.8 RBD Act.
note: Under s.8-10 RBD Act the head of the institution is the informant for institutional births. Post-2023 amendment, the report is filed digitally on the CRS portal.

action: Create account on CRS portal (dc.crsorgi.gov.in) with parents' Aadhaar and file the birth-reporting form.
note: The Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2023 (in force 01-Oct-2023) made digital registration via CRS mandatory; Aadhaar of parents is captured. For home births the parent is the informant under s.8.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Registrar of Births & Deaths, Nagar Nigam)
action: Receive the reporting form and documents; scrutinise for completeness and attach supporting proofs.
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued; informant re-submits missing documents.
note: Required documents: hospital birth-report/discharge summary, parents' Aadhaar/ID and address proof, and (some ULBs) marriage proof of parents. Registrar's office is the urban local body (Municipal Corporation).

post_name: Registrar of Births & Deaths (Nagar Nigam — designated Health Officer / Chief Medical Officer)
action: Verify the reported particulars against records and enter the event in the birth register.
on_reject: Objection recorded; informant asked to reconcile particulars or produce affidavit.
note: s.7 & s.12 RBD Act: the Registrar for an urban area is the officer designated by the Municipal Corporation (commonly the Health Officer / CMO or a designated corporation official).

action: Register the birth in the statutory register — this is the decisive registration act.
on_reject: If refused, escalate to the District Registrar of Births and Deaths.
note: s.12 RBD Act: on registration the Registrar shall give, free of charge, an extract of the prescribed particulars. Registration within 21 days carries no fee.

action: Generate and issue the QR-verified digital birth certificate to the informant.
on_reject: On non-delivery within the guaranteed period, invoke the State Right-to-Public-Services appeal (First Appellate Authority).
note: s.12/s.17 RBD Act read with 2023 amendment: the digital certificate carries a QR code and is the single proof of date of birth for those born on/after 01-Oct-2023. UP delivery guaranteed under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011.

action: For reporting after 21 but within 30 days, register on payment of the prescribed late fee.
on_reject: Escalate to District Registrar.
note: s.13(1) RBD Act. UP prescribed late fee at this tier is nominal (approx. Rs 2). This step applies only when the 21-day window was missed.

post_name: District Registrar of Births & Deaths / Additional District Magistrate
action: For reporting after 30 days but within one year, grant written permission to register on late fee plus notarised affidavit.
on_reject: Apply to a First Class / Executive Magistrate for an order (see next step).
note: s.13(2) RBD Act: requires written permission of the prescribed authority, prescribed fee (approx. Rs 5 in UP), and an affidavit before a notary public. Prescribed authority in UP is typically the District Registrar / ADM.

action: For births not registered within one year, pass a magisterial order directing registration on payment of fee.
on_reject: Revision before the District Magistrate; thereafter writ jurisdiction of the High Court.
note: s.13(3) RBD Act: registration after one year requires an order of a Magistrate of the First Class or Presidency Magistrate; in UP this is routed through the SDM / Executive Magistrate.

post_name: First Appellate Authority (designated officer, UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam)
action: On delay or refusal, hear the citizen's appeal and direct issuance within the guaranteed period.
on_reject: Second appeal to the Second Appellate Authority; parallel RTI to the CMO / District Registrar; complaint to State Chief Registrar (Births & Deaths) / Directorate.
note: UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 provides a tiered appeal with penalty on the defaulting designated officer. Grievance also lies to the District/Chief Registrar under the RBD Act.

action: At government delivery point, give BCG, OPV-0, Hep B birth dose before discharge; open MCP card.
time_limit: Hep B birth dose within 24 hours of birth
note: At a government hospital/CHC/PHC the ward nurse or ANM administers birth doses and issues the Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card. If born at a private facility or at home, birth doses/card may not have been given - proceed to step 2. UP runs a pilot (Sambhal/Jhansi) placing govt-supplied BCG/OPV-0/Hep B and U-WIN registration inside private delivery facilities.

post_name: Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) / Auxiliary Nurse Midwife (ANM)
action: Ask your area's ASHA/ANM for the immunization session site, day and time for your address.
note: Free UIP vaccines are delivered at the nearest sub-centre, PHC/Urban PHC, Anganwadi centre and at Village Health & Nutrition Day (VHND) outreach sessions - in Uttarakhand/NHM these are held on Saturdays at the Anganwadi, Panchayat Bhawan or school. The ASHA maintains the due-list of children and mobilizes them; the ANM runs the session. They are the ground-truth source for the exact site/day.

action: Optionally self-register the child on the U-WIN Citizen app/web portal and book the nearest session.
on_reject: If self-registration fails, the ANM registers the child on-site at first visit.
note: U-WIN is the MoHFW national electronic immunization registry. Self-registration via the U-WIN Citizen mobile app or web portal lets you search centres by district/sub-district/PIN, book a slot, and later download a QR e-Vaccination Certificate and generate the child's ABHA. Optional - a walk-in without prior registration is fully allowed; the ANM can register you at the session.

action: At the session, register the child in U-WIN, issue/update the MCP card, record dose and next due-date.
note: No referral, income proof or prior appointment is required - free routine immunization is a walk-in entitlement. Bring the child and, if available, the birth certificate/hospital discharge slip or any ID. The MCP card (paper) plus the U-WIN digital record together form the immunization record you present at every later visit and for school admission.

action: Verify the child's age/eligibility and vaccinate free per the National Immunization Schedule.
note: National Immunization Schedule primary series: OPV/Pentavalent/Rota/PCV/fIPV at 6, 10 and 14 weeks; MR-1 & JE-1 (in endemic districts) and PCV booster at 9-12 months; DPT booster 1, OPV booster, MR-2 and JE-2 at 16-24 months. All 12-disease UIP vaccines are free at government points.

action: Track the due-list and remind you of each next dose; U-WIN sends SMS reminders 3 days prior.
note: Being late does not disqualify the child - catch-up is available and decided by the vaccinator per national guidelines. The MCP card prints due-dates and U-WIN sends automated SMS reminders three days before each due dose.

action: If turned away or a card/dose is refused, raise it with the PHC Medical Officer.
on_reject: If unresolved, escalate to the District Immunization Officer / CMO (step 8).
note: The Medical Officer in charge of the PHC/Urban PHC supervises the ANM/ASHA and the routine-immunization sessions in the block and can direct issuance of the card or the due vaccine.

post_name: Chief Medical Officer (CMO) / District Immunization Officer (DIO)
action: If still unresolved, approach the District Immunization Officer in the CMO's District Health Office.
on_reject: State NHM Routine Immunization division; national health helpline 104/1075 can also route the grievance.
note: The District Immunization Officer (DIO), housed in the office of the Chief Medical Officer (the district-health lead office for this task), owns UIP delivery for the district - vaccine supply, session planning and grievances. A district health helpline or the national 104/1075 helpline can also route the complaint.

action: Issue Medical Certificate of Cause of Death (Form 4/4A) to the family.
note: RBD Act s.10 + Rules: attending doctor/hospital certifies cause of death on Form 4 (institution) or Form 4A (non-institutional). In Uttarakhand urban areas the CMO is a designated District Registrar for deaths.

action: Report the death and submit the death report (Form 2) within 21 days.
time_limit: 21 days from date of death (RBD Act s.10 + Rules)
note: RBD Act ss.8-9 fix the informant: for a house death, the head of household or nearest relative; for a hospital/institution, the medical officer in charge; for cremation/burial ground, the person in charge.

post_name: Registrar of Births and Deaths (Municipal Health Officer / designated ward-zone Registrar)
action: Receive Form 2, medical cause-of-death certificate, and ID/address proofs at counter or e-district portal.
note: In a municipal-corporation area the Registrar function sits in the corporation Health Dept (a designated Registrar/Sub-Registrar). Documents: Form 2, Form 4/4A, proof of identity of deceased (Aaadhaar), informant ID and address proof, cremation/burial receipt. Apply via UP eDistrict (edistrict.up.gov.in) or Uttarakhand eServices / CRS portal.

action: Verify documents against Form 4/4A and informant particulars for completeness.
on_reject: Return application for missing/discrepant documents; informant re-submits.
note: Registrar checks the report against the medical certificate; if reported within 21 days registration is normal and no fee is charged for entry.

post_name: Prescribed Authority (Additional District Registrar / District Registrar)
action: For delay of 30 days to 1 year, grant written permission on affidavit plus prescribed late fee.
time_limit: Applies only when reported after 30 days and within 1 year (RBD Act s.13(2))
on_reject: Escalate to District Registrar; ultimately magistrate route under s.13(3).
note: RBD Act s.13: 21-30 days = small prescribed late fee only; 30 days-1 year = registered only with written permission of the prescribed authority + affidavit before a notary + prescribed fee. Skip this step if reported within 21 days.

action: For delay beyond 1 year, pass an order authorising registration after verifying correctness.
time_limit: Applies only when reported after 1 year (RBD Act s.13(3))
on_reject: Revision/representation to District Magistrate.
note: RBD Act s.13(3): a death not registered within one year is registered only on an order of a Magistrate of the First Class / Executive Magistrate after verifying correctness, on payment of the prescribed fee. Skip if within 1 year.

action: Enter the death in the register and record it on the national CRS portal.
on_reject: Refusal to register is appealable to the District Registrar / Chief Registrar under RBD Act s.25.
note: This is the operative decision that completes registration. Post-2023 Amendment (in force 1 Oct 2023) registration on the Centre's Civil Registration System (crsorgi.gov.in) is mandatory and data is shared with the Registrar General of India.

action: Issue the death certificate (digital or physical) free of charge to the informant.
time_limit: Within 7 days of completing registration (RBD Act s.17)
note: RBD Act s.17 (as amended 2023): Registrar gives, free of charge and not later than 7 days, a certificate to the person who gave information under s.8/s.9, electronically or otherwise. Additional/duplicate copies carry a small prescribed fee.

action: Issue additional certified copies on request against the prescribed per-copy fee.
time_limit: State RTS schedule where notified (UP Janhit Guarantee / Uttarakhand RTS)
on_reject: First appeal (see step 11) if copy not delivered within the RTS time limit.
note: Extra copies are searched and issued under RBD Act s.17; digitally certified copies are downloadable from the UP eDistrict / Uttarakhand eServices portal.

action: Process corrections/cancellations of entries on written application with proof.
on_reject: Refusal appealable to District Registrar under RBD Act s.25.
note: RBD Act s.15 + Rules: clerical/material errors (name, date, spelling) are corrected or cancelled by the Registrar with a margin entry on documentary proof; not by erasing the original entry.

post_name: First Appellate Officer (Additional District Magistrate / designated officer under state RTS)
action: Hear appeal where service is refused or exceeds the RTS time limit; direct delivery.
time_limit: File within 30 days of rejection or expiry of the stipulated time limit (UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011, s.5-6)
on_reject: Second appeal to the Second Appellate Authority within 60 days.
note: Under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (and the Uttarakhand Right to Service Act), the First Appellate Officer may order the designated officer to deliver within a fixed period; a second appeal lies within 60 days.

post_name: Second Appellate Authority (Commissioner / senior officer under state RTS)
action: Decide second appeal and may impose penalty on the defaulting designated officer.
time_limit: File within 60 days of the first-appeal decision (UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011)
on_reject: Parallel remedy: RBD Act s.25 appeal to Chief Registrar; or writ/RTI.
note: The RTS statute empowers the second appellate authority to penalise the designated officer for unjustified delay/refusal, closing the accountability loop.

action: Register applicant on national UDID portal (swavlambancard.gov.in) or via e-District UP; select disability type, upload Aadhaar/photo.
note: UP applicants may also route through divyangjanUP / e-District CSC counters; application is federated to the national UDID system. 2024 amendment allows applying at any hospital (not only government).

post_name: Chief Medical Officer (CMO) office / Medical Authority
action: Receive online application, verify applicant data and documents, forward to the concerned district hospital for assessment.
on_reject: Deficiency memo to applicant via portal for correction/resubmission.
note: CMO office is the designated medical authority node that controls the district hospital assessment queue in the UDID workflow.

post_name: Chief Medical Officer (CMO) office / Medical Authority
action: Assign the relevant specialist(s) and schedule an assessment slot or refer to a periodic disability assessment camp.
note: Walk-in vs. appointment vs. camp-only varies by district and disability type; multi-disability cases may need several specialists on different days.

post_name: Medical Officer (MO) / Specialist (orthopaedic, ENT, ophthalmic, psychiatrist etc.)
action: Clinically examine the person in-person; run required diagnostics (audiometry, X-ray, vision, IQ) for the claimed disability.
note: In-person presence of the person with disability is required; assessment is clinical, not documentary. Specialist matched to disability category.

action: Determine disability type and assess percentage against the national gazetted assessment guidelines; record opinion on portal.
note: Percentage assessed per the Ministry's notified 'Guidelines for assessment of the extent of specified disability' under the RPwD Act.

post_name: Medical Board (chaired by CMO / Medical Superintendent + specialists)
action: Review the specialist finding, confirm disability type and final percentage; decide certificate eligibility.
on_reject: Rejection reasons conveyed to applicant via Form VIII within one month; appeal within 90 days (see step 9).
note: Board is the standard approving body; a single specialist may suffice for straightforward categories, but the Medical Board is the deciding authority.

action: Authenticate the assessment on the UDID portal; digitally sign and generate the Disability Certificate (Form V).
note: Certificate becomes downloadable once the CMO/medical authority authenticates it in the portal; integrated with DigiLocker in UP e-District.

action: Generate the UDID number and print the UDID card (Form VI / colour-coded Form VII); dispatch centrally, usually by post.
time_limit: Certificate + UDID card within 3 months of application (Rule 18, as amended 2024)
note: Colour band by severity: White (<40%), Yellow (40-79%), Blue (80%+). Physical card dispatch may lag certificate download by additional weeks.

post_name: State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities / notified Appellate Authority
action: Hear appeal against rejection or disputed percentage; order re-assessment or revision.
time_limit: Appeal within 90 days of rejection (Form VIII)
on_reject: Further remedy before the State/Chief Commissioner for PwD (s.75/s.80 RPwD Act) or the courts.
note: Rejection notified via Form VIII within one month; appeal filed under s.59(1) RPwD Act, 2016. First-stop grievance desk may be the District Disability office / DM; portal-technical issues route to the national UDID helpdesk.

post_name: Applicant / Citizen (self, or via Jan Seva Kendra CSC operator)
action: Register on UDID portal swavlambancard.gov.in; fill personal, disability and address details.
note: Free. In UP the assisted route is the Jan Seva Kendra / CSC or e-District. An enrolment number is issued to track status. Portal is run by DEPwD. Confidence high on portal/route.

action: Upload identity proof, address proof, photograph, and any existing medical/disability records; select district hospital/CMO.
note: Aadhaar, photo, address proof and prior medical records. Applicant selects the designated assessing hospital / CMO office in their district. Grounded in DEPwD UDID application flow.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (UDID cell, District Hospital / CMO office)
action: Receive and scrutinise application on portal; verify documents; assign a medical assessment date.
on_reject: Application returned on portal for correction/resubmission of documents.
note: The application lands with the designated medical authority selected in Step 2. RPwD Rules 2017 Rule 18(1): medical authority verifies information before assessment.

post_name: Medical Officer (MO) / Specialist (orthopaedic, ophthalmologist, ENT, psychiatrist as per disability)
action: Examine applicant on assigned date; measure impairment and quantify disability percentage per notified guidelines.
note: Assessment per Gazette Notification S.O. 76(E), 04.01.2018. Single specialist for some categories (e.g. locomotor); a full Medical Board for multiple/intellectual/mental disability. Applicant brings originals.

post_name: Medical Board (chaired by Chief Medical Officer (CMO) / Civil Surgeon)
action: Deliberate on assessment, fix disability category and percentage, and decide eligibility for certification.
time_limit: Within one month of receipt of application (RPwD Rules 2017, Rule 18(3))
on_reject: If found ineligible, reasons conveyed in Form VIII within one month; appeal under RPwD Act s.59 within 90 days of rejection (Rule 18(4)).
note: The decisive step. CMO chairs the district Medical Board. Certificate issues only if the person is a person with a specified disability (benefits generally require >=40%). Confidence high (statutory).

post_name: Chief Medical Officer (CMO) / Medical Superintendent (competent medical authority)
action: Generate the disability certificate in Form V / VI / VII and digitally sign it on the portal.
time_limit: Within one month of receipt (RPwD Rules 2017, Rule 18(3))
note: Form VII for a single disability; Form V/VI for multiple disabilities. Certificate is valid across the country (RPwD Act s.58(3)). Digitally signed by the competent medical authority.

post_name: UDID Cell, Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD, Central)
action: Generate the UDID number and card centrally after certificate approval; enable e-card download.
note: UDID card carries a unique ID, disability type and percentage; single nationally-valid credential. E-card downloadable immediately; generated centrally by DEPwD after the CMO approves. Confidence high on structure.

action: Dispatch the physical PVC UDID card to the applicant's address by post; e-card remains downloadable.
time_limit: Physical card typically 30-60 days (administrative, not statutory)
note: The downloadable e-card is the operative credential; the PVC card follows by post. Turnaround for the physical card is administrative, not a statutory day-count. Confidence high on route, medium on exact turnaround.

post_name: Applicant / Citizen (via portal track-status or Jan Seva Kendra)
action: Track status by enrolment number; if stalled beyond one month, escalate to the CMO / designated hospital.
note: Rule 18(3) fixes one month for issuance; delay beyond it is escalable to the CMO/Medical Superintendent, then the portal grievance channel. Confidence high on the one-month peg.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Fix the first date of hearing on the application after receiving it
time_limit: Within 3 days of receipt of the application (Section 12(4))
note: Section 27: JMFC/Metropolitan Magistrate within whose jurisdiction the woman resides/works, respondent resides, or cause of action arose, has jurisdiction.

post_name: Appellate Authority designated by State Government (Directorate of Medical & Health Services / State Medical Board)
action: Hear appeal against rejection or wrongly-assessed percentage; re-decide the certification.
time_limit: Appeal within 90 days of rejection (RPwD Rules 2017, Rule 18(4) read with Act s.59)
on_reject: Further complaint of denial of rights lies with the State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (RPwD Act, ss.79-80); UP: cmsdivyangjan.up.gov.in.
note: Section 59 vests appeal in a State-designated appellate authority; the 90-day window is fixed by Rule 18(4). Exact appellate body name varies by state notification (UP: State Medical Board / DGMH). Confidence high on provision, medium on exact body.

post_name: State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (statutory)
action: Hear complaints of deprivation of rights or non-implementation; direct remedial action on the certificate/benefits.
on_reject: Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities at the Centre (RPwD Act, ss.74-75).
note: Statutory grievance forum under RPwD Act ss.79-80 for denial of rights (distinct from the medical-percentage appeal). UP court: cmsdivyangjan.up.gov.in. Confidence high (statutory).

action: Prerequisite: hold a valid 40%+ disability certificate / UDID from the medical board.
on_reject: Apply/re-assess for disability certificate at the CMO's medical board before proceeding.
note: Certificate already held per the citizen input; UDID (Unique Disability ID) card is preferred where available.

action: Issue/verify income certificate confirming family income within the rural/urban ceiling.
note: UP ceiling: Rs 46,080 rural / Rs 56,460 urban per year. Income certificate is a required enclosure; issued via Lekhpal/SDM through the e-district service.

action: Countersign/issue the income and residence (domicile) certificates for the applicant.
note: Income certificate is issued by Lekhpal/SDM; domicile proof also required. These are prerequisite certificates, not the pension decision.

action: Register and submit disability-pension application online on the state pension portal with enclosures.
note: UP: sspy-up.gov.in, choose 'Divyang and Leprosy Pension' > Apply Online. Uttarakhand: ssp.uk.gov.in disability grant form. Enclose disability certificate, Aadhaar, domicile, income certificate, bank passbook, photo. Guardian may apply where the applicant cannot.

action: Field-verify applicant's disability, residence and circumstances at village/ward level.
on_reject: Applicant may correct/resubmit documents flagged at verification.
note: Rural verification by Gram Panchayat / block functionary; in urban areas a municipal/ward-level officer performs the equivalent field check. Portal notes verification by 'Gram Panchayat/Block/District Social Welfare Office'.

action: Verify the application at block level and forward with recommendation to the district office.
on_reject: Deficiency memo to applicant; resubmit corrected documents.
note: Block-tier verification/forwarding on the pension portal before district scrutiny; exact routing varies by district.

post_name: District Disability Welfare Officer / District Social Welfare Officer (Zila Divyangjan/Samaj Kalyan Adhikari)
action: Scrutinise application and documents; validate disability certificate against issuing medical board.
on_reject: Return for correction; applicant may re-submit or seek grievance redress on the portal.
note: The District Disability/Social Welfare Officer runs the scheme locally (UP: Divyangjan Sashaktikaran Adhikari; Uttarakhand: DSWO at Vikas Bhawan). This is the substantive district scrutiny step.

post_name: District Disability Welfare Officer / District Social Welfare Officer
action: Sanction the pension and enrol the beneficiary on the pension roll.
on_reject: Rejection is appealable to the next-higher authority (Director/Deputy Director, Divyangjan Sashaktikaran / Samaj Kalyan) and via the portal grievance cell.
note: This is the decision step. Sanctioning authority is the designated district welfare officer; some districts route final approval through the District Magistrate/Collector-level committee.

action: Set up and credit recurring monthly pension to the Aadhaar-linked bank account by DBT.
note: UP Rs 1,000/month paid quarterly (Rs 3,000/quarter); Uttarakhand Rs 1,200-1,500/month. Direct Benefit Transfer, no intermediary; may include arrears from sanction date.

post_name: District Disability Welfare Officer / District Social Welfare Officer
action: Conduct periodic re-verification (annual continued-eligibility/life check) to keep pension active.
on_reject: Payment paused pending re-verification; beneficiary completes eKYC/life certificate to reinstate.
note: Annual re-confirmation of eligibility is required; portals support eKYC for continuation.

post_name: Appellate authority (Right to Public Services / Sewa Adhikar)
action: Hear appeal on delay past service deadline or on rejection; direct sanction if due.
on_reject: Further appeal to second appellate authority / ombudsman (Lokayukt) or the High Court.
note: UP: escalation under the Uttar Pradesh Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 where the service is notified. Grievance/status functions exist on both state pension portals. Whether pension sanction is a notified guaranteed service should be confirmed locally.

post_name: Protection Officer (District, appointed under Section 8 PWDVA)
action: Aggrieved woman reports abuse; Protection Officer records Domestic Incident Report (Form I) and informs her of rights
on_reject: May approach a registered service provider, police, or file directly with the Magistrate - PO route is optional (Section 4)
note: Section 4/9 & Rule 5: any person may inform the Protection Officer; woman may also go direct to court. DIR is Form I under Rule 5.

post_name: Protection Officer / Station House Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Forward the Domestic Incident Report to the Magistrate and to the local police station; assist woman in getting legal aid
on_reject: Woman/counsel may file the application directly without waiting for the DIR
note: Section 9 & Rule 8/10: PO forwards copies of DIR to Magistrate and police officer in charge; ensures free legal aid under Legal Services Authorities Act.

post_name: Aggrieved Person / Protection Officer (applicant to court)
action: File application for protection order to the Magistrate in Form II under Section 12, seeking reliefs sought
note: Section 12 & Rule 6: application in Form II may be filed by the aggrieved person, a Protection Officer, or any other person on her behalf. No court fee.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Consider Domestic Incident Report; grant interim or ex parte protection order if satisfied prima facie of violence
time_limit: May be granted at first hearing / same day (Section 23)
on_reject: Aggrieved person may lead further evidence at the full hearing; final order can still grant relief
note: Section 23: Magistrate may pass interim orders and, on an affidavit (Form III), ex parte orders under ss.18-22 before the respondent is heard.

action: Serve notice of the hearing (and any interim order) on the respondent as directed by the Magistrate
time_limit: Within a maximum of 2 days, or further time allowed by the Magistrate (Section 13 & Rule 12)
on_reject: Substituted service may be ordered by the Magistrate if the respondent evades service
note: Section 13 & Rule 12: notice served by Protection Officer; a declaration of service by the PO is proof of service.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Hold hearing; both parties appear, evidence and counter-affidavit considered; respondent may contest
time_limit: Endeavour to dispose of the application within 60 days of the first hearing (Section 12(5))
note: Section 12(5): Magistrate shall endeavour to dispose of every application within 60 days of the first hearing. May direct counselling (Section 14) or welfare expert (Section 15).

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Decide the application and, if satisfied domestic violence occurred, pass the Protection Order under Section 18
on_reject: Appeal to the Court of Session within 30 days from service of the order (Section 29)
note: Section 18 protection order prohibits further violence, contact, entry, etc. Magistrate may also pass residence (19), monetary relief (20), custody (21), compensation (22) orders.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: Sign the order; supply free certified copies to the aggrieved person and respondent
note: Section 24: copies given free of cost to parties, Protection Officer, and the police station in charge of the area. Protection order remains in force until aggrieved person applies for discharge (Section 25).

post_name: Protection Officer / Station House Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Serve/enforce the order; on breach, register cognizable offence and arrest respondent
note: Section 31: breach of a protection order is a cognizable, non-bailable offence - up to 1 year imprisonment and/or fine up to Rs.20,000. Copy sent to SHO under Section 24.

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class / Metropolitan Magistrate
action: On application, modify, alter or revoke the order on change of circumstances
on_reject: Appeal to Court of Session within 30 days (Section 29)
note: Section 25(2): either party may apply for alteration/modification/revocation on change in circumstances. Protection order continues until discharged.

action: Hear appeal against the Magistrate's order and confirm, modify or set it aside
time_limit: Appeal to be filed within 30 days of service of the order (Section 29)
on_reject: Further remedy by revision/writ before the High Court (outside PWDVA)
note: Section 29: appeal lies to the Court of Session within 30 days from the date the order is served on the aggrieved person or the respondent, whichever is later.

action: Identify area DISCOM and apply online via Jhatpat portal (upenergy.in) declaring sanctioned load in kW.
note: In UP the licensee is a UPPCL DISCOM for the applicant's zone (PVVNL Meerut, MVVNL Lucknow, PuVVNL Varanasi, DVVNL Agra, KESCO Kanpur) or a private licensee (NPCL/Torrent); in Uttarakhand it is UPCL. Application also accepted at Jan Suvidha / e-Suvidha centres or the sub-division office. Domestic (DS) load selectable 1 kW to 500 kW.

action: Upload ID proof, ownership/occupancy proof, photograph; pay application fee (Rs 100 APL / Rs 10 BPL).
note: Ownership proof per Supply Code: registered sale deed / partition deed / succession or heir (vasiyat) certificate; occupant may use rent agreement + owner NOC. Fee amounts are the Jhatpat scheme rates; the refundable security deposit and line/service charges come later via the demand note, not at application.

action: Register application, verify documents for completeness, generate application/registration number.
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued; applicant re-submits missing documents; deemed-registration on completeness.
note: Scrutiny/registration at the DISCOM sub-division (Vidyut Vitran Khand) serving the address. Incomplete applications are returned with a checklist rather than rejected outright.

action: Conduct site/feasibility inspection: confirm load, nearest distribution pole/point, and technical feasibility.
on_reject: Infeasibility recorded with reasons; applicant may contest via CGRF (step 10).
note: Applicant suggests up to three preferred inspection dates on the portal. The DISCOM JE (Avar Abhiyanta) is the field officer; assesses whether existing mains suffice or a line extension/transformer augmentation is needed - this determines the release timeline.

post_name: Sub-Divisional Officer / Assistant Engineer (SDO/AE, Upkhand Adhikari)
action: Prepare cost estimate and issue the demand note specifying charges and security deposit.
on_reject: Dispute estimate before Executive Engineer or CGRF; excess/erroneous charges refundable.
note: Demand note (Supply Code cl. 4.x) itemizes processing/registration fee, refundable security deposit, and any service-line / system-loading (development) charges. The statutory release clock in step 8 runs from the applicant's compliance with this demand note.

action: Pay demand-note charges and security deposit online or at the sub-division cash counter.
note: Payment (compliance of the demand note) is the trigger event for the statutory release timeline in step 8.

post_name: Executive Engineer (Adhishasi Abhiyanta / XEN, Vidyut Vitran Khand)
action: Sanction the connection and authorize meter installation at the approved load.
on_reject: Appeal refusal/improper conditions to CGRF, then Electricity Ombudsman.
note: This is the decisional approval: the Executive Engineer (or delegated SDO for small DS loads) sanctions supply under the DISCOM's duty to supply (Electricity Act s.43). Sanctioning authority varies with load slab per DISCOM delegation.

action: Install meter and energize the connection within the regulated release period.
time_limit: 7 days (DS, no mains extension) / 15 days (minor extension) from demand-note compliance; longer where new infrastructure needed
on_reject: Delay beyond the standard entitles the applicant to compensation under Standards of Performance / Rights of Consumers Rules 2020; escalate via steps 9-11.
note: UP Electricity Supply Code 2005 cl. 4.15/4.16: supply within 7 days for DS/NRS where no augmentation/erection/extension of distribution mains is required, 15 days where minor extension needed. Uttarakhand (UERC Supply Code) allows up to ~90 days for fresh connections needing infrastructure. Jhatpat scheme markets ~10 days end-to-end.

post_name: Executive Engineer (Adhishasi Abhiyanta / XEN, Vidyut Vitran Khand)
action: First-level grievance: register delay/refusal complaint via 1912 or the sub-division/circle grievance cell.
on_reject: If unresolved, approach the Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (step 10).
note: Internal DISCOM redressal (toll-free 1912 / 1800-180-8752) is the first tier before the statutory forum. Not a separate statute; part of the DISCOM's consumer-service obligations.

action: Adjudicate the grievance if internal redressal fails or times out.
time_limit: Resolution generally within the period set by CGRF Regulations 2022; ~90 days outer limit
on_reject: Approach the Electricity Ombudsman (Vidyut Lokpal) within 30 days of the CGRF order or expiry of the resolution period.
note: Constituted under UPERC (Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum & Electricity Ombudsman) Regulations, 2022 (notified 21-07-2022), at circle and company level. In Uttarakhand the equivalent CGRF operates under UERC regulations.

action: Final statutory appeal: hear representation against the CGRF order or unresolved grievance.
time_limit: File within 30 days of CGRF order or expiry of its resolution period
on_reject: Order binding on the licensee; further recourse only via writ jurisdiction of the High Court.
note: Electricity Ombudsman appointed by UPERC under Electricity Act 2003 s.42(6) and the 2022 Regulations. Delay compensation under the Electricity (Rights of Consumers) Rules, 2020 / Standards of Performance may also be claimed here.

action: Constitute entity; obtain PAN, GST, bank account; confirm worker headcount and power load cross Factories Act threshold
note: Prerequisite, not part of the licence. Factories Act Sec. 2(m) 'factory' trigger: 10+ workers with power or 20+ without power; below this the factory licence may not be required.

action: Gather evidence: FBO name/address, bill, wrapper, retained food sample, photos, date and time.
note: Physical sample and bill materially support later formal sampling and any Section 40 self-analysis right.

post_name: Local Development Authority / SIDCUL Estate Office (Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) where gram-panchayat/revenue land is involved)
action: Confirm industrial land use / zoning and obtain building-plan approval for the site
on_reject: Reapply after re-zoning / land-use change; land-use appeal to the development authority
note: Approving body depends on whether the plot sits inside a SIDCUL/State Industrial Development Corporation estate, a municipal area, or gram-panchayat/revenue land. SDM named where revenue-land conversion is needed.

post_name: Member Secretary, Uttarakhand Environment Protection & Pollution Control Board (UEPPCB)
action: Apply for Consent to Establish (CTE) under Water Act Sec.25 and Air Act Sec.21 before construction
time_limit: Statutory limit set by state RTS notification; commonly 30-120 days by category (not confirmed this session)
on_reject: Appeal to the Uttarakhand Appellate Authority under the Water/Air Acts; then National Green Tribunal
note: Red/Orange/Green/White categorisation drives documents and timeline. CTE must precede the Factories-Act licence; White-category units are often exempt/self-declared.

post_name: Chief Inspector of Factories, Directorate of Factories, Boilers, Labour & Employment (Uttarakhand)
action: Submit factory building plans and layout for prior approval before constructing the manufacturing area
time_limit: As notified under Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011 (exact days not confirmed this session)
on_reject: Resubmit corrected plans; appeal within Directorate, then State Government / RTS appellate route
note: Factories Act Sec. 6 and Uttarakhand Factories Rules require prior approval of plans/layout (state plan-approval form) before construction.

action: File Sec.7 occupier notice and the application for registration and licence with prescribed fee
note: Application on Form No. 2 (Model/most state rules); occupier notice under Sec. 7. Fee scaled by worker count and installed HP/kW per the Uttarakhand Factories Rules fee schedule (exact form numbers/fees are state-rule specific).

post_name: Inspector of Factories, Directorate of Factories (Uttarakhand)
action: Scrutinise application, occupier/manager particulars and approved plan; inspect premises for compliance
on_reject: Comply with deficiency notice and re-submit
note: Verification of safety, health and welfare provisions and consistency with the approved layout before the licence is granted.

post_name: Chief Inspector of Factories, Directorate of Factories (Uttarakhand)
action: Register the factory and grant the licence to operate under the Factories Act, 1948
time_limit: As notified under Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011 (exact days not confirmed this session)
on_reject: Appeal under Factories Act Sec. 6(2)/state rules to the State Government within the prescribed period; RTS appeal for delay
note: This is the core decision. Licence typically issued on Form No. 4 (Model/most state rules), renewable; the registration number is allotted here. This step is the actual grant of the factory licence.

post_name: Regional Officer, Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC) and Regional PF Commissioner, EPFO
action: Register the establishment for ESI and EPF once employee thresholds are crossed
time_limit: ESI/EPF registration is time-bound from the date coverage is attracted
on_reject: Rectify and re-register; appeal under ESI Act / EPF & MP Act to the respective appellate forum
note: ESI Act 1948 applies at 10+ employees (in covered areas); EPF & MP Act 1952 at 20+ employees. Registration via the unified Shram Suvidha portal.

post_name: Registering Officer, Contract Labour (Labour Department, Uttarakhand)
action: Register the principal employer under the Contract Labour Act if using contractor-supplied workers
on_reject: Appeal to the appellate officer under the Contract Labour (R&A) Act, 1970
note: Only if contract workers engaged (threshold 20+ contract workers per the Central Act, subject to state amendment). Also register under Shops & Establishments / labour-welfare rules as applicable.

post_name: Chief Fire Officer, Uttarakhand Fire & Emergency Service (and Director of Boilers where a boiler is run)
action: Obtain Fire NOC and boiler registration/certification only where the process triggers them
on_reject: Rectify fire-safety/boiler deficiencies and reapply; departmental appeal
note: Triggered clearances only: Fire NOC; boiler registration under the Boilers Act 1923; plus Legal Metrology, FSSAI/Drug/explosives/hazardous-chemical licences depending on the product. Skip those that do not apply.

post_name: Member Secretary, Uttarakhand Environment Protection & Pollution Control Board (UEPPCB)
action: After construction and installation, obtain Consent to Operate (CTO) before starting production
time_limit: As notified under Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011 (exact days not confirmed this session)
on_reject: Appeal to the Uttarakhand Appellate Authority under Water/Air Acts; then National Green Tribunal
note: CTO under Water Act Sec.25 / Air Act Sec.21 is distinct from the CTE taken at Step 3. CTE is not permission to run production - CTO is the final environmental go-live gate.
