post_name: Designated Officer / Nodal Officer, Single Window Facilitation (Invest Uttarakhand) and Right to Service appellate authorities
action: Escalate any approval that exceeds its notified time limit through single-window then RTS appeal
on_reject: First appeal to the designated first appellate authority, then the Uttarakhand Right to Service Commission; ultimately a writ petition in the Uttarakhand High Court for unreasonable delay
note: Front the whole flow through the Invest Uttarakhand single-window portal. Delay remedy runs under the Uttarakhand Right to Service (Sewa Ka Adhikar) Act, 2011: designated officer -> first appellate authority -> RTS Commission (exact named authorities not confirmed this session).

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Give oral/written info of the cognizable offence; SHO must record and register the FIR.
time_limit: Immediate (no waiting period for cognizable offences)
on_reject: If SHO refuses, escalate in writing to the Superintendent of Police (Step 4) under BNSS S.173(4).
note: BNSS S.173: officer in charge must reduce cognizable-offence information to writing, read it back, and register the FIR. Info can be given electronically (e-FIR), signed within 3 days. For specified sexual offences a woman officer records the statement.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Register FIR in station records and issue a free copy of the FIR to the complainant.
note: BNSS S.173(2): the informant is entitled to a copy of the recorded information free of cost. Filing an FIR carries no fee.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: For offences punishable 3-7 years, may hold a 14-day preliminary enquiry with senior officer's permission before FIR.
on_reject: Enquiry cannot indefinitely delay registration; if suppressed, escalate to SP (Step 4).
note: BNSS S.173(3): with prior permission of an officer not below DSP rank, the SHO may conduct a preliminary enquiry (within 14 days) into whether a prima facie cognizable case exists for 3-7 year offences. For grave offences FIR must be registered forthwith.

post_name: Superintendent of Police (SP) / Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP)
action: Send substance of complaint in writing by registered post to SP if SHO refused to register.
on_reject: If SP takes no action, approach the Judicial Magistrate under BNSS S.175(3) (Step 6).
note: BNSS S.173(4): a person aggrieved by refusal to record information may send its substance in writing, by post, to the SP; in commissionerate cities the equivalent authority is the DCP. Keep the postal receipt as proof.

post_name: Superintendent of Police (SP) / Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP)
action: If satisfied a cognizable offence is disclosed, investigate personally or direct an officer to register and investigate.
on_reject: If SP declines, move the Judicial Magistrate under BNSS S.175(3) (Step 6).
note: BNSS S.173(4): on being satisfied that a cognizable offence is disclosed, the SP shall either investigate the case or direct a subordinate to do so, which includes registering the FIR.

action: File a written application before the jurisdictional Magistrate to order police to register the FIR and investigate.
on_reject: If application is not entertained, file a private complaint under BNSS S.223 (Step 8) or a High Court writ.
note: BNSS S.175(3): a Magistrate empowered under S.210 may, after enquiry and considering the S.173(4) submission to the SP, order investigation - i.e. direct registration of the FIR. This is the core court remedy; office class = district court. Designation is Judicial Magistrate First Class (not in the standard revenue-post list).

action: Order the officer in charge to register the FIR and investigate; require an action-taken report.
note: Under BNSS S.175(3) the Magistrate directs the police to register and investigate; this compels the refusing station to act.

action: Alternatively, take the matter as a private complaint - record complainant and witness statements and proceed.
note: BNSS S.223 (formerly CrPC S.200): the Magistrate may take cognizance of the offence on complaint, examine the complainant on oath, and proceed without police - an alternative route if S.175(3) registration is not sought.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Parallel option: file e-FIR / online complaint via UP Police CCTNS citizen portal or dial 112.
on_reject: If the online portal only logs a 'complaint' (not an FIR), still pursue Steps 1-7.
note: UP Police CCTNS Citizen Portal (cctnsup.gov.in) offers e-FIR for specified categories (e.g. unknown-accused / vehicle theft) and complaint registration; emergency number is 112. e-FIR availability and whether it counts as a formal FIR varies by category and state - not a substitute for the statutory route above.

post_name: Superintendent of Police (SP) / Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP)
action: For misconduct by the refusing officer, complain to Police Complaints Authority / SHRC / Jansunwai (IGRS).
on_reject: High Court writ (mandamus) as last resort to compel registration.
note: Refusal to register an FIR for a cognizable offence is itself an actionable dereliction. UP grievance route: Jansunwai/IGRS portal; State Human Rights Commission; State Police Complaints Authority. Designation for oversight body is outside the standard revenue-post list.

post_name: Regional Transport Officer / Assistant Regional Transport Officer (RTO/ARTO)
action: Approve and issue the Learner's Licence on passing, usually same day.
on_reject: Refusal without cause appealable to the Regional/Deputy Transport Commissioner, then State Transport Commissioner.
note: Learner's Licence issued as Form 3 (confirmed on Sarathi: 'Print Learner Licence (Form3)'); valid 6 months. This decides the LL request.

post_name: Station House Officer (SHO), jurisdictional police station
action: Give oral/written account; officer must reduce it to writing, read back, obtain signature, register FIR
on_reject: If refused, escalate under s.173(4) to the Superintendent of Police (step 4)
note: For a cognizable offence, registration is mandatory under s.173(1) BNSS — no discretion; Lalita Kumari v. Govt. of U.P. (2014) 2 SCC 1 makes registration compulsory. Give jurisdiction over the place of offence, but s.173(1) applies 'irrespective of the area' (zero-FIR): any station must register and transfer later.

action: Issue the free copy of the registered FIR to the complainant immediately
on_reject: Demand the copy in writing; non-issue is itself grounds for the s.173(4) SP complaint
note: s.173(1) BNSS entitles the informant to a copy of the FIR free of cost, forthwith.

post_name: Deputy Superintendent of Police (permission) / Station House Officer (enquiry)
action: Where FIR not immediately registered, verify whether a 14-day preliminary enquiry lawfully applies before deciding registration
on_reject: If enquiry not concluded or wrongly invoked, escalate to SP under s.173(4)
note: s.173(3) BNSS permits a preliminary enquiry ONLY for offences punishable 3-7 years, with prior permission of a DSP-level officer, capped at 14 days. It is not a general escape from mandatory registration. NOTE: for a purely non-cognizable offence, s.174 BNSS applies instead — police only enter it in a register and cannot investigate without magistrate order; the refusal-to-register FIR framing is specific to cognizable offences.

post_name: Superintendent of Police (SP) — or Deputy Commissioner of Police (DCP) in a Police Commissionerate
action: Send substance of the information in writing by (registered) post; SP must investigate or direct a subordinate
on_reject: If SP remedy yields no result, apply to the Judicial Magistrate under s.175(3) (step 6)
note: s.173(4) BNSS: a person aggrieved by the SHO's refusal sends the substance in writing, by post, to the SP; if satisfied a cognizable offence is disclosed the SP shall investigate or direct a subordinate who then has SHO powers. Registered post gives proof of submission. Recourse to the SP is now a MANDATORY precondition before the magistrate route.

post_name: First Appellate Officer (DIG range) then Second Appellate Officer (Zonal ADG), U.P. Police — Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam
action: Optionally lodge a service-guarantee appeal for non-action within the stipulated time
time_limit: First appeal within 30 days; second appeal within 60 days
on_reject: Second appeal to Zonal ADG; independent of, and parallel to, the s.175(3) magistrate route
note: U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 gives time-bound service delivery with a First Appeal (30 days) and Second Appeal (60 days). UP Police designate the First Appellate Officer (DIG) and Second Appellate Officer (Zonal ADG) for police-service grievances; useful for non-action/delay but does not itself compel FIR registration — the statutory compulsion route is s.175(3).

post_name: Judicial Magistrate First Class (JMFC), jurisdictional court
action: File an affidavit-supported application asking the Magistrate to direct police to register and investigate
on_reject: If the Magistrate declines, pursue a private complaint under s.223 (step 8) or revision/High Court under Article 226/482
note: s.175(3) BNSS: the Magistrate empowered under s.210 may, after considering the affidavit under s.173(4) and the police's submission on their refusal, order investigation. Attach the SHO complaint, the SP (s.173(4)) complaint and proof of both (Priyanka Srivastava v. State of U.P. (2015) requires the supporting affidavit). Exhausting the SP remedy is a precondition.

action: Lodge complaint on FSSAI Food Safety Connect portal or app; receive unique concern number.
note: foscos.fssai.gov.in/consumergrievance or the Food Safety Connect mobile app; routes to state Designated Officer/FSO. Concern number enables tracking.

action: Sanction and grant the trade licence, or reject with reasons.
time_limit: Per corporation's notified SLA under UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 (indicative ~7-30 days).
on_reject: Written rejection with reasons; appeal to the first appellate authority under UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011, then second appellate authority.
note: Nagar Ayukt is the licensing authority under the UP Municipal Corporation Act 1959; power is frequently delegated to a Zonal/Additional/Deputy Commissioner.

action: Issue the trade licence on payment of the assessed fee; deliver certificate / download.
note: Licence issued on the e-Nagar Sewa portal or at the counter after fee payment.

action: If SLA lapses or service refused, escalate to first then second appellate authority.
on_reject: First appellate authority, then second appellate authority under the 2011 Act; parallel Jansunwai grievance / RTI for status and delay reasons.
note: Verified escalation lever: Jansunwai-Samadhan portal (jansunwai.up.nic.in) sends deadline-lapse reminders and pushes stalled municipal grievances up the chain.

action: Renew the annual licence before expiry to keep the trade lawful.
note: Trade licences are typically annual; running without a current licence invites penalty or sealing. Renew on the same portal/office.

action: Apply for Learner's Licence via Parivahan Sarathi portal or at jurisdictional RTO; submit Form 2.
note: Form 2 application with Form 1 self-declaration of fitness; Form 1A doctor's medical certificate required for transport vehicles or applicants above the age threshold (commonly 40+, varies by state - flag). Grounded in CMV Rules 1989 R.10-11.

action: Upload proof of age and address, photos; pay the statutory learner-licence fee online or at counter.
note: Exact fee is state-specific under the U.P. Motor Vehicles Rules 1998 (flag). Documents per CMV Rules 1989 R.4/R.10.

post_name: Regional Transport Officer / Assistant Regional Transport Officer (RTO/ARTO)
action: Verify submitted documents and schedule the learner's test slot.
on_reject: If documents deficient, applicant is asked to re-submit; escalate to RTO officer in charge.
note: RTO/ARTO is the licensing authority designation under the state Transport Department (real post title; outside the provided revenue/panchayat list - noted). Slot booking confirmed on Sarathi portal (LL Test Slot Booking).

action: Sit the computerized learner's test on traffic signs, road rules and safety at the RTO.
on_reject: On failure, re-book and re-take the test after the permitted interval.
note: Pass mark commonly ~60% but state-specific (flag). Some states allow a supervised at-home online test. Confirmed as a service on Sarathi (Mock Test / LL Test).

action: Wait the mandatory minimum 30 days after LL issue; then apply for permanent DL within the 6-month LL validity.
time_limit: Minimum 30 days after LL issue; apply within 180 days (LL validity)
on_reject: If the 6-month LL lapses, re-do Stage 1 (fresh learner's licence).
note: Statutory 30-day minimum interval under CMV Rules 1989 (R.15). Applying beyond LL validity requires a new LL.

action: Apply for permanent Driving Licence via Form 4 on Sarathi or at the RTO.
note: Form 4 is the statutory DL application form (CMV Rules 1989 R.14; confirmed as 'New Driving Licence' on Sarathi).

action: Pay the driving-licence and driving-test fee; book a driving-test slot.
note: DL fee plus test/slot fee; exact amounts state-specific under U.P. Motor Vehicles Rules 1998 (flag). Slot booking confirmed on Sarathi (DL Test Slot Booking).

action: Conduct and evaluate the practical driving test at the RTO track or Automated Driving Test Track.
on_reject: On failure, applicant re-books and re-tests after a short waiting period (e.g. ~1 week - varies, flag).
note: Applicant arranges a vehicle of the class applied for. ADTT (Automated Driving Test Track) increasingly mandatory in larger cities (flag). MVI is the real statutory testing designation (outside the provided list - noted).

post_name: Regional Transport Officer / Assistant Regional Transport Officer (RTO/ARTO)
action: Approve the permanent Driving Licence on a passed test.
on_reject: Refusal without cause appealable to Regional/Deputy Transport Commissioner, then State Transport Commissioner.
note: Licensing authority approves issue after the MVI's pass report. This decides the permanent DL request.

action: Print and dispatch the smart-card Driving Licence by post, or hold for collection.
note: Permanent DL valid 20 years or until age 50, whichever earlier; the MV (Amendment) Act 2019 revised age brackets and renewal rules (flag). Print DL confirmed on Sarathi.

action: Escalate service delay/refusal up the chain; invoke Right-to-Public-Services deadline where scheduled.
time_limit: As scheduled under the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (where the DL service is notified)
on_reject: Designated appellate officer under the Janhit Guarantee Act; Parivahan grievance channel for portal/technical failures.
note: Escalation ladder: RTO officer in charge to Regional/Deputy Transport Commissioner to State Transport Commissioner (department head). RtPS coverage, notified deadline and appellate officer are state-specific (flag).

action: Register the death and obtain the death certificate from panchayat (rural) or municipal registrar (urban).
on_reject: Apply with late-registration affidavit; escalate to District Registrar (Births & Deaths).
note: Registration of Births and Deaths Act 1969. Urban: apply to Municipal Commissioner (Nagar Ayukt)/registrar instead. Nothing downstream proceeds without this.

action: File varasat application online at vaad.up.nic.in (RCCMS) or e-District/e-Sathi, or at Jan Seva Kendra.
on_reject: Resubmit; use CSC/Jan Seva Kendra assistance if portal upload fails.
note: UP routes agricultural-land inheritance as varasat (mutation) through the Revenue Court system (RCCMS), NOT a standalone certificate. For dues/pension file the Surviving Member Certificate on e-District in parallel.

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Supervise tapping of the main, laying the service pipe, fitting the meter, connecting the drain to the sewer manhole; restore road.
note: Work done by the department or an empanelled licensed plumber under JE supervision; meter reading and billing then commence in the applicant's name.

action: Attach death certificate, applicant ID/address proof, heir list affidavit, khatauni/khasra extract, ration card.
on_reject: Add missing documents on portal query; affidavit of all legal heirs on stamp paper is commonly required.
note: Exact list varies by tehsil and by purpose (property mutation vs dues). Self-declaration naming ALL heirs is central.

action: Conduct field inquiry (mauka) verifying death, heirs, and possession; file spot-verification report.
on_reject: If report adverse, submit objections/evidence before the Tehsildar; request re-inquiry.
note: Lekhpal is the UP revenue field officer; this is the step that most often causes delay.

action: Publish public notice inviting objections from other claimants to the inheritance.
on_reject: If objection filed, case is contested and heard as a revenue suit (vaad) before the court.
note: UP Revenue Code 2006 §§33-34: notice/objection period before recording succession in records.

action: Hear the varasat case and pass order recording legal heirs in the revenue records (khatauni).
on_reject: Appeal to SDM (Assistant Collector), then ADM/Collector, then Commissioner, then Board of Revenue.
note: UP Revenue Code 2006 §35. Tehsildar/Naib-Tehsildar sits as the revenue court; order effects the mutation (dakhil-kharij).

action: Issue the Surviving Member / legal-heir certificate for claiming dues, pension and benefits.
on_reject: Appeal to SDM; file delay complaint under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011.
note: Parallel e-District instrument to the property mutation; downloaded from the portal after Tehsildar approval.

action: Download the mutated khatauni and certificate; present to bank, employer, insurer and revenue office.
note: For bank deposits/shares, debts or contested property, institutions may still require a court succession certificate (Indian Succession Act 1925) — a separate judicial track (district court), not the collectorate.

action: If stalled or refused, escalate: SDM/RDO, then Collector/DM, then First/Second Appellate Officer under RTS.
on_reject: File time-bound-service complaint under UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 (penalty on defaulting officer); CM/district grievance portal.
note: Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 makes notified services time-bound with a First and Second Appellate Officer and penalty for delay.

action: Update portal status and issue verification acknowledgement/status to the landlord.
note: Most CCTNS portals show a downloadable acknowledgement/'no adverse report' status rather than a formal certificate.

action: Adult of a rural household applies (plain paper, prescribed form, or orally) to the Gram Panchayat for household registration.
note: You register as a HOUSEHOLD, not an individual; the card covers all adult members. Oral application must be reduced to writing by the GP. Application may also be made to the Programme Officer. Schedule II, para 1-2.

action: Gram Panchayat (Secretary with Gram Rozgar Sahayak) verifies applicants are local residents and adults of the household.
on_reject: Complaint to Programme Officer (BDO) at block if verification is arbitrarily withheld.
note: Light residence/adult-membership check only. NOT a means test - MGNREGA is universal for rural households, not income-targeted. Schedule II, para 3.

action: Gram Panchayat registers the household and issues the Job Card with photos and a unique registration number, free of cost.
on_reject: Non-issue is a grievance: escalate to Programme Officer (BDO) at block; then District Programme Coordinator; then MGNREGA Ombudsman.
note: Job Card must be issued within 15 days of registration, free of cost. This is the decisive step that creates the entitlement. Schedule II, para 4-5. Keep the card - it is presented to demand work.

action: Card-holder submits a written application for work to the Gram Panchayat or Programme Officer and obtains a dated receipt.
on_reject: If receipt is refused, apply directly to the Programme Officer (BDO); the demand can be sent by post.
note: Having the card is NOT the same as having work. The dated receipt starts the legal 15-day clock for the guarantee. Minimum 14 days' continuous work may be sought. Schedule II, para 6-8.

action: Programme Officer (usually the BDO) allots work and directs the Gram Panchayat to provide employment within 5 km of residence.
on_reject: Failure to provide work triggers unemployment-allowance liability (step 6); complaint to District Programme Coordinator / Ombudsman.
note: Employment must be provided within 15 days of the work-demand (or the later date sought). Work ordinarily within 5 km; beyond 5 km, extra wages payable. Section 3; Schedule II. In UP the Programme Officer is generally the BDO.

action: If no work provided within 15 days, Programme Officer sanctions daily unemployment allowance to the applicant.
on_reject: Non-payment of allowance is itself a grievance: escalate to District Programme Coordinator, then MGNREGA Ombudsman.
note: Unemployment allowance is the enforcement teeth of the guarantee; it is a State liability. Rate is State-notified (not below one-fourth of wage for first 30 days, one-half thereafter). Section 7; Schedule II.

action: If GP refuses registration or the card, escalate the grievance to the Programme Officer at the Block.
on_reject: Next level: District Programme Coordinator.
note: The Programme Officer (Section 15) is the supervisory authority over Gram Panchayats for MGNREGA at the block. In UP this is the BDO.

post_name: District Programme Coordinator (District Magistrate / CEO Zila Panchayat)
action: District Programme Coordinator reviews unresolved grievances on registration, card issue, work, or wage/allowance.
on_reject: Next level: MGNREGA Ombudsman for the district.
note: District Programme Coordinator (Section 14) is the District Magistrate / CEO of the Zila Panchayat - the district-level authority. Real designation noted as it falls outside the standard post list.

action: Independent Ombudsman receives and adjudicates complaints on non-registration, card denial, delayed work, or unpaid allowance/wages.
on_reject: Parallel routes: State MGNREGA helpline and Social Audit before the Gram Sabha (Section 17).
note: Every district has an independent MGNREGA Ombudsman (Ombudsman Rules/Guidelines, 2009) for grievance redressal. Real designation noted as it is outside the standard post list.

action: Report the lapse; get it logged in the school complaint register / SMC.
on_reject: Escalate to the School Management Committee and Block Education Officer
note: Under MDM Rules 2015 the School Head and School Management Committee (SMC, with parent members) are responsible for the meal and first-level redress; use the mandated info-board helpline if displayed. Uncertainty: register/SMC functioning varies by school.

post_name: Block Education Officer (BEO) / Khand Shiksha Adhikari
action: Escalate unresolved complaint; BEO directs supply, cook-cum-helper, or vendor correction.
on_reject: Escalate to District Basic Shiksha Adhikari / District Education Officer
note: Cook-cum-helper and food supply are administered at block level (Block/Nagar MDM in-charge under the Khand Shiksha Adhikari). Uncertainty: exact MDM nodal designation differs by district.

action: Refer supply/vendor or Gram Panchayat-side lapse to the block-level MDM monitoring committee.
on_reject: Escalate to district level
note: The block/mandal-level MDM monitoring committee (MDM Rules 2015) meets fortnightly; the BDO can act on Gram-Panchayat-administered cook/supply arrangements. Optional parallel tier.

post_name: District Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) / District Education Officer (DEO) - District MDM/PM POSHAN Nodal Officer
action: File written district complaint; DEO orders inspection and directs corrective action.
on_reject: Escalate to District Magistrate / Collector and State Project Director
note: In UP the district MDM authority is the Basic Shiksha Adhikari; the DEO/BSA is district nodal officer for PM POSHAN and convenes district inspection. This is the substantive district office for the task.

action: Chairs district MDM monitoring committee; orders inspection, penalizes vendor, enforces compliance.
on_reject: Approach District Grievance Redressal Officer (NFSA) or State Food Commission
note: The district-level MDM monitoring committee (MDM Rules 2015) meets monthly and is chaired by the DM/Collector, the senior authority who can order inspection and corrective action - the effective decision point once school and block fail.

action: File statutory NFSA grievance; DGRO investigates and recommends relief within time-bound process.
on_reject: Appeal to the State Food Commission
note: NFSA 2013 (Sec. 14) makes the mid-day meal a legal entitlement enforceable via the District Grievance Redressal Officer; the State Food Commission (Sec. 15-16) hears appeals and can impose penalty on defaulting officials. Confirm the district's designated DGRO locally.

post_name: State Project Director / State Nodal Officer, PM POSHAN (Samagra Shiksha / Education Dept.)
action: Escalate systemic or unresolved complaint; state directorate directs district and vendor action.
on_reject: File on CPGRAMS or approach State Food Commission
note: State PM POSHAN directorate (UP: Mid-Day Meal Authority / Prayavaran; Uttarakhand: Samagra Shiksha). Many states run a toll-free MDM helpline - number is state-specific; verify locally. Uncertainty: helpline existence/number varies.

post_name: CPGRAMS Grievance Officer (Dept. of School Education & Literacy)
action: File online grievance at pgportal.gov.in; get tracking ID; grievance routed to department.
on_reject: Use the CPGRAMS appeal option after closure if feedback is 'Poor'
note: CPGRAMS is the central 24x7 grievance portal; routes to the relevant department with a tracking number and an appeal path. Parallel channel usable at any time. Timeline is a general target, not a statutory MDM limit.

post_name: Food Safety Officer / Designated Officer (FSSAI - state Food Safety Dept.)
action: For hygiene/adulteration/illness, lodge a food-safety complaint; officer inspects and can prosecute.
on_reject: Escalate to the Food Safety Commissioner of the state
note: Parallel track under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 where the issue is contamination, adulteration, or illness. If any child fell ill, also involve the Medical Officer (MO) / CMO immediately. Use only for food-safety-specific complaints.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Jal Kal Vibhag, Nagar Nigam)
action: Confirm your service provider is the Nagar Nigam Jal Kal Vibhag (Jal Sansthan) for household connections in your city.
note: Under the U.P. Water Supply & Sewerage Act 1975, Jal Nigam lays trunk mains while the Jal Sansthan/Jal Kal Vibhag (merged into Nagar Nigam w.e.f. 01.04.2009) gives household connections. In a few cities Jal Nigam still handles connections directly — confirm at the counter or e-Nagarsewa portal.

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Check whether a distribution water main / public sewer already runs near your plot, or if only a new-line extension is possible.
note: The single biggest branch. A tap/sewer connection is sanctionable only where a main already passes; if no line is laid, it becomes a slower network-extension (often colony/group or developer-coordinated) request under the Act.

action: Gather sale deed/allotment letter, latest house-tax receipt/property ID, approved building plan, Aadhaar, photo.
note: Exact checklist varies per corporation; occupancy/completion certificate may also be asked. Confirm the current list on the e-Nagarsewa UP portal or the zonal Jal Kal office.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Jal Kal Vibhag, Nagar Nigam)
action: Submit the water-connection (and sewer-connection) form with documents; pay the application/scrutiny fee.
on_reject: Resubmit with corrected documents; deficiency memo issued at counter.
note: File in person at the zonal Jal Kal office or online via the state e-Nagarsewa UP portal (e-nagarsewa.up.gov.in), where the corporation has enabled it. (Nivesh Mitra is for business approvals, not household connections.)

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Inspect the site, confirm main proximity, fix pipe/ferrule/meter size, and prepare the demand note.
note: The JE (assisted where needed by the Assistant/Junior Engineer) records feasibility and specifications that drive the charge computation.

post_name: Assistant Engineer (Sahayak Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Assess and issue the demand: connection/tap fee, road-cutting/restoration charge, security deposit, meter cost, sewer charge.
note: Charges are levied under the U.P. Water Supply & Sewerage Act 1975 and the corporation's schedule; amounts are city-specific.

action: Deposit the assessed demand (tap fee, deposit, meter, road-cutting, sewer charge) at counter/treasury/online.
note: Retain the challan/receipt; sanction is issued only after full payment.

post_name: Executive Engineer (Adhishasi Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Sanction the connection and issue the work order authorising tapping of the main and sewer.
on_reject: Appeal to General Manager (Jal Kal) / Municipal Commissioner; then First Appellate Authority under U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011.
note: The zonal Executive Engineer is the competent sanctioning authority in the Jal Kal Vibhag (each of the department's zones is headed by an Executive Engineer).

post_name: Junior Engineer (Avar Abhiyanta), Jal Kal Vibhag
action: Obtain road-cutting NOC (PWD/Nagar Nigam roads dept) if the main lies across a public road.
note: Required where tapping needs excavation of a public carriageway; restoration charge already collected in the demand.

post_name: General Manager (Jal Kal) / Municipal Commissioner (Nagar Ayukt)
action: Escalate delay/refusal to the GM Jal Kal, then the Municipal Commissioner, via the corporation grievance channel.
on_reject: CM Helpline 1076; IGRS jansunwai.up.nic.in.
note: First administrative escalation above the Executive Engineer within the Nagar Nigam.

post_name: First / Second Appellate Authority (U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011)
action: If a notified service-delivery timeline was breached, appeal to the designated First then Second Appellate Authority.
on_reject: State/District Consumer forum; or writ petition; Lokvani/IGRS grievance channels.
note: The Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 provides a designated officer + First/Second Appellate Authority and penalties for default. The specific guaranteed day-count for a water/sewer connection is not verified here — confirm the notified schedule locally.

action: Heir files mutation-on-inheritance application at the tehsil / Devbhoomi e-district portal with heirship proof.
note: Documents: father's death certificate, proof of relationship/legal-heir (or registered will if testate), current khatauni copy, and applicant ID. Intake is via the local Lekhpal/Patwari circle; exact online vs counter channel varies by tehsil (Devbhoomi/e-district Uttarakhand). Succession basis (intestate under applicable personal law vs will; ancestral vs self-acquired) governs which heirship proof is required.

action: Records the death and claimed succession and reports the change of possession for entry.
note: Section 34, U.P. Land Revenue Act 1901 (as adopted by Uttarakhand) obliges reporting of every succession/transfer of possession; the Lekhpal prepares the report and updates the khasra/field record accordingly.

action: Public notice / proclamation issued at the village level inviting objections from co-heirs and interested parties.
time_limit: typically 15–30 days notice window (not a confirmed statutory figure)
note: Because inheritance succession can be contested, the proposed mutation is notified and objections invited from other potential heirs/neighbours. If none is filed within the window, it proceeds as an uncontested (undisputed) mutation. The 15–30 day window is practice-reported, not confirmed from a named provision.

action: Naib Tehsildar / Tehsildar attests the undisputed inheritance entry and orders it mutated into the heir's name.
time_limit: no confirmed statutory day-count for rural revenue mutation; urban/municipal dakhil-kharij carries a 30-day Right-to-Service limit
on_reject: Appeal the revenue order upward: Tehsildar/SDM → Additional District Magistrate (Collector) → Commissioner → Board of Revenue (apex revenue authority, Uttarakhand).
note: For an undisputed succession, a Naib Tehsildar attests the entry; the Tehsildar-level revenue officer (under the SDM / District Collectorate) passes the order. This is the 'who decides' answer for the ordinary uncontested case. Municipal (Nagar Nikay) mutation of urban land is a separate track under the Uttarakhand Right to Service Act 2011 with a notified 30-day limit.

action: If any co-heir/third party objects, mutation is registered as a contested revenue case and heard as a mini-trial.
on_reject: Appeal the reasoned order: SDM → Additional District Magistrate/Collector → Commissioner → Board of Revenue.
note: Mutation proceedings are judicial; a disputed succession is decided by the Revenue Officer of Tehsildar rank in revenue-court capacity, with parties, evidence and a reasoned order after opportunity of hearing. No order on a disputed mutation without hearing the parties. Contested cases have no meaningful fixed time limit.

action: On approval, corrects the entry in the khatauni and the digitized (Devbhoomi) record.
note: The Lekhpal carries the ordered mutation into both the manual khatauni and the digital record. A common failure point is an order passed but the digital record not updated.

action: Heir obtains a fresh khatauni copy showing their name to confirm the mutation was carried through.
on_reject: If the record is not updated after the order, escalate to the SDM and then the District Collectorate / District Magistrate.
note: Verify via the Devbhoomi / e-district Uttarakhand portal or a certified tehsil copy. Reminder for the citizen: mutation updates the fiscal/possession record — it does NOT confer or prove title. If ownership itself is disputed among heirs, revenue authorities will not resolve title (that needs a civil suit / partition) and may decline to mutate until settled.

action: If the Lekhpal or Tehsildar delays or refuses, escalate to the SDM and up the revenue hierarchy.
on_reject: Full revenue appeal chain: Tehsildar → SDM → Additional District Magistrate/Collector → Commissioner → Board of Revenue; a Right-to-Service delay complaint for the municipal-track mutation goes to the designated first/second appellate authority under the Uttarakhand Right to Service Act, 2011.
note: Escalation ladder: SDM, then District Collectorate / District Magistrate for administrative delay, and the statutory revenue appeal chain for a passed order. Exact RTS appellate tiers apply to the notified municipal service and are jurisdiction-specific for the rural revenue track (unverified from a named provision).

action: Citizen applies online (UPPCL 'Jhatpat' / UPCL portal) or offline at DISCOM sub-division for a new domestic LT connection.
note: Counterparty is the DISCOM (UPPCL discoms/KESCO in UP; UPCL in Uttarakhand), not the secretariat. Office-class is set to secretariat-department (Energy/Power Dept as policy host), but the applicant-facing lead office is the DISCOM sub-division. Online single-window is primary; offline at sub-division is the degradation-resilient fallback.

action: Receive application and fee; check enclosed documents (ID, ownership/occupancy proof, photo, load, contractor test report if required) for completeness.
on_reject: Applicant is asked to cure deficiencies / resubmit; no adverse decision on merits at this stage.
note: Exact mandatory-document list and whether a licensed-electrician wiring/test report is required varies by load slab and circle. Treat document specifics as medium confidence.

action: Inspect premises; verify feasibility and whether existing network serves the load or a line/transformer extension is needed.
note: Branch point per Electricity Act 2003 s.43/s.46: service-line-only cases are fast; network-extension cases trigger a separate estimate and longer statutory window.

action: Issue demand note stating security deposit, service-line/connection charges and any system-loading/development charge.
on_reject: Refusal to supply is appealable; s.43 imposes a duty to supply within the statutory period.
note: SDO/AE (real DISCOM designation, outside the supplied post list). Security deposit governed by Electricity Act 2003 s.47; charges recoverable under s.46 and the state Supply Code. Amounts vary by circle/load - low confidence on figures.

action: Pay the demand note (security deposit + charges) online or at the sub-division cash counter.
note: The statutory clock for release of connection generally runs from complete application / paid demand note under the state Supply Code.

action: Sanction the standard domestic load connection after payment is confirmed.
time_limit: ~7-15 days from complete application where no extension is required (UP/Uttarakhand Supply Code norm)
on_reject: Wrongful refusal/delay -> Executive Engineer, then CGRF and Electricity Ombudsman (step 9).
note: SDO/AE is sanctioning authority for standard domestic LT load; higher loads route to the Executive Engineer or above. Exact statutory day-count is fixed by UPERC/UERC Supply Code and Standards of Performance and varies by revision - treat the range as approximate.

action: Install/commission meter and energize the service line; record meter and consumer account details.
note: Delay beyond the Standards-of-Performance timeline may attract compensation payable to the consumer under the state SoP regulations.

action: First internal escalation for delay/refusal beyond statutory time; may also sanction higher-load connections.
on_reject: Proceed to CGRF (step 9).
note: Executive Engineer / XEN is the real DISCOM divisional head (outside the supplied post list). Also the sanctioning authority above the SDO's load threshold.

post_name: Consumer Grievance Redressal Forum (CGRF) / Electricity Ombudsman
action: Adjudicate unresolved grievance (delay, wrongful refusal, charges); Ombudsman hears appeals from CGRF.
on_reject: State ERC (UPERC / UERC); Consumer Protection forum as a parallel route; compensation under Standards of Performance regulations.
note: CGRF and Electricity Ombudsman are mandated under Electricity Act 2003 s.42(5)-(6); Ombudsman appointed by UPERC (UP) / UERC (Uttarakhand). Right-to-Service escalation (UP Janhit Guarantee / Uttarakhand Sewa Ka Adhikar Adhiniyam) applies where the service is notified.

action: Confirm eligibility/category and that no member holds an existing ration card anywhere
note: Categories: AAY (poorest) / Priority Household / State non-subsidized. Eligibility criteria are state-NFSA-specific; verify locally.

action: Obtain surrender/deletion certificate if splitting name from a prior household card
note: A person may appear on only one card; deletion from the old card (a separate FCS transaction) is commonly required before a fresh card. Requirement varies by district.

action: File new-card application with documents via e-district / URCMS portal or CSC kiosk
note: UP: fcs.up.gov.in / edistrict.up.gov.in (Rural/Urban/Migrant form). Uttarakhand: URCMS uk.smartpds.nic.in or offline at DSO. Docs: Aadhaar of all members, residence proof, HoH photo, bank/LPG details; income declaration if category requires.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (DSO office / Tehsil Supply)
action: Scrutinize application, check documents and completeness, forward for verification
on_reject: Deficiency memo; applicant resubmits corrected form
note: Data-entry/dealing clerk at the Tehsil Supply Office / District Supply Office is the intake point in the e-district workflow.

post_name: Supply Inspector / Food Supply Inspector (Ration/Food Inspector)
action: Conduct field verification of residence and household composition, submit report
on_reject: Adverse report; application returned to clerk with reasons
note: The FSI/Supply Inspector physical verification is the usual source of delay. In rural areas the Lekhpal / Patwari may co-verify residence.

action: Review verification report and recommend the case for sanction
on_reject: Returns case for re-verification or rejection with reasons
note: Intermediate approval tier in the e-district routing (data operator -> FSI -> Assistant DSO -> DSO). Title varies by district; some districts route sanction through the Tehsildar / SDM as designated officer.

action: Sanction the ration card and digitally sign / approve issuance
time_limit: ~15 days (UP Janhit Guarantee ration-card window); 15-30 working days (Uttarakhand)
on_reject: Rejection order stating reasons; appealable under state Right-to-Service / Janhit Guarantee Act
note: DSO (a district-collectorate food-wing officer) is the sanctioning/digital-sign-off authority. In some UP districts the Tehsildar/SDM is the notified designated officer for this service.

action: Generate the NFSA card, link it to a Fair Price Shop, release e-ration card
note: Card downloadable from the state portal (e-ration card) and mapped to an FPS for grain drawal; name added to the NFSA eligibility list.

post_name: First Appeal Officer (Janhit Guarantee) / Additional District Magistrate
action: Hear appeal if service not delivered within the notified time or rejected
time_limit: File within 30 days of rejection/expiry (UP JGA Sec. 6)
on_reject: Second appeal to the next designated appellate officer under the Act
note: UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 gives a time-bound first-appeal remedy; Uttarakhand equivalent under its Right to Service Act 2011.

action: Escalate PDS grievance under NFSA if statutory remedies exhausted
on_reject: Onward to State Food Commission under NFSA Sec. 15
note: NFSA 2013 Sec. 14-15: DGRO then State Food Commission is the food-specific redressal track, parallel to the Right-to-Service appeal.

action: Confirm eligibility: age 60+, state resident, income below ceiling / BPL, not drawing another pension.
note: UP SSPY income ceiling: Rs 46,080/yr rural, Rs 56,460/yr urban. Uttarakhand: income up to Rs 4,000/month from all sources or BPL. Age threshold is firmly 60+ (draft's 65 is incorrect for the state scheme). 'No regular income' qualifies but must be evidenced by an income certificate or BPL card.

action: Assemble documents: age proof, residence/domicile, income certificate or BPL, Aadhaar, bank passbook, photo.
note: Bank account must be Aadhaar-linked for DBT. In Uttarakhand a family register (rural, issued by VPDO) or ration card (urban) is required. Income certificate is itself an e-district/RTPS service if not already held.

action: Issue income certificate through e-District if applicant lacks one; establishes the below-ceiling income fact.
on_reject: Re-apply with supporting income evidence; income-certificate refusal is itself appealable under the state RTPS/Janhit Guarantee schedule.
note: Prerequisite, not part of the pension sanction chain. The income certificate is the key gating document confirming 'no regular income'. Handled by the Tehsil revenue chain (Lekhpal -> Tehsildar/SDM).

action: Submit online application on state Integrated Pension Portal (sspy-up.gov.in / ssp.uk.gov.in) or via CSC.
note: Corrects draft: intake is the online state portal (or Common Service Centre / Apuni Sarkar e-services in Uttarakhand), NOT the Collectorate counter or the Gram Panchayat form. Applicant selects 'Old Age Pension' -> 'Apply Online', fills personal/bank/income fields, uploads documents, submits. UMANG and myScheme also route here.

action: Field-verify residence and income at village level; in Uttarakhand list is placed before open Gram Sabha.
on_reject: Discrepancy returned to applicant for correction/resubmission before higher forwarding.
note: Uttarakhand rural chain: Gram Panchayat Development Officer (VPDO) -> Assistant Social Welfare Officer recommend; beneficiaries are selected in an open Gram Sabha meeting. This is the local-verification layer the draft was unsure about.

action: Verify rural applications via official login and forward recommended cases to the sanctioning officer.
on_reject: Returned to lower level / applicant if particulars fail verification.
note: On SSPY, the BDO verifies rural applications with a login ID and forwards to the District Social Welfare Officer. In Uttarakhand the BDO recommends onward to the DSWO.

action: Verify urban applications (SDM / Sub-District Officer login) and forward recommended cases for sanction.
on_reject: Returned for correction if urban residence/income particulars fail verification.
note: SSPY urban verification is done by SDM / SDO (in Uttarakhand, Assistant Social Welfare Officer + Sub-District Magistrate). Parallel to step 6 depending on rural vs urban applicant; only one of steps 5-7's paths applies.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer / District Probation Officer (DPO)
action: Scrutinise the verified case and sanction the pension; approval initiates DBT enrolment.
time_limit: Approx. 30-60 days from complete application (per state RTPS / Janhit Guarantee service window)
on_reject: Applicant may seek review by the District Magistrate / Collector and file a statutory appeal under the UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act if the time limit lapses or the case is wrongly rejected.
note: This is the actual sanctioning authority, correcting the draft's uncertainty: the District Social Welfare Officer (in UP the District Probation Officer / DPO handles pension sanction) signs, NOT the District Magistrate case-by-case. The DM/Collector is supervisory and appellate. Post-name uses the real official designations.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer / District Probation Officer (DPO)
action: Release sanctioned pension in quarterly installments via NEFT/DBT to the Aadhaar-linked account.
note: Corrects draft: payment is quarterly (four installments/year) by NEFT/DBT once funds are released by the state directorate (HQ Lucknow in UP), not monthly cash/money order. Nominal monthly rate: UP ~Rs 1,000, Uttarakhand Rs 1,500.

action: Hear appeals against rejection/delay and enforce time-bound delivery under the state Right-to-Service Act.
time_limit: Statutory appeal window under UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act
on_reject: Second appeal to the designated appellate authority under the RTPS Act; parallel grievance via CM Helpline (1076) / state social-welfare grievance portal.
note: Escalation ladder, grounded: (1) review by District Social Welfare Officer / DPO; (2) District Magistrate / Collector; (3) statutory RTPS appeal under the Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam if the service window lapses; (4) CM Helpline / department grievance portal. Confirms the Collectorate's real role here is supervisory/appellate, as the draft suspected.

action: Confirm whether family's name is already on the Gram Panchayat's PMAY-G Permanent Wait List (SECC/Awaas+).
on_reject: If name absent, proceed to Awaas+ 2024 self-survey (step 2) to seek fresh inclusion.
note: PWL is drawn from SECC 2011 deprivation data plus Awaas+ returns, displayed at Gram Sabha. Being on the list, not filing a form, is the gate. Check status at pmayg.nic.in.

post_name: Head of Family (self-survey applicant) / Awaas+ enumerator
action: Register the household via the AwaasPlus 2024 app: self-survey with Aadhaar OTP/face auth, or assisted survey by enumerator.
on_reject: If self-survey not possible (no smartphone), request assisted survey by the Panchayat enumerator/Sachiv.
note: Awaas+ 2024 survey (launched 17 Sept 2024; app self-survey from Jan 2025) enrols families left out of SECC 2011. Eligibility (Aug 2024): kachcha house of 0-2 rooms, household income <= Rs. 15,000/month, Aadhaar-seeded bank account, no prior housing benefit; two-wheeler/refrigerator no longer disqualify. Survey window is periodically extended - confirm current deadline locally.

action: Capture four-side geo-tagged photos of the existing kachcha house and submit family, income, asset, and bank details.
on_reject: Poor GPS/photo failures require retaking geo-tagged photos before submission.
note: Form captures Aadhaar of head + all members, house specs, toilet status, income, land holding, Aadhaar-linked bank account. Applicant receives a registration/application number by SMS on submission.

action: Conduct field verification: fresh geo-tagged photos and cross-check of self-declared income, assets, and house condition.
on_reject: If details fail verification, applicant may correct/re-submit or raise the matter at Gram Sabha (step 6).
note: Tier-1 (Panchayat) verification, typically ~30-60 days. Data recorded in AwaasSoft MIS. Time limit is a programmatic target, not statutory.

action: Scrutinise Panchayat-endorsed list; run duplicate and automatic-exclusion checks against AwaasSoft MIS.
on_reject: Wrongful exclusion at block level can be contested at Gram Sabha (step 6) and escalated to Project Director, DRDA.
note: Tier-2 (Block) verification. BDO validates against the modified exclusion criteria before the district finalises.

action: Publicly present eligible list for objections; ratify additions/corrections by resolution and set priority ranking.
on_reject: An omitted-but-eligible family raises an appeal-against-exclusion here; the Gram Sabha resolution feeds back to Block/District.
note: Gram Sabha ratification is the mandated social-audit step. Automated priority scoring weights kachcha-house severity and SC/ST/widow/disabled/minority vulnerability. This is the key escalation route for genuinely eligible but omitted BPL families.

post_name: Project Director, District Rural Development Agency (DRDA)
action: Finalise the verified list and update the Permanent Wait List (PWL) on AwaasSoft MIS.
on_reject: Fund-release or finalisation delays are escalated to the CDO (Chief Development Officer), who heads the DRDA at district level.
note: Tier-3 (District) finalisation. DRDA is chaired by the CDO in UP; the Project Director runs day-to-day PMAY-G administration. Post title 'Project Director, DRDA' is the real UP designation (outside the supplied post list).

action: Generate the sanction order as funds reach the block and the family moves up the PWL; notify by SMS.
on_reject: If sanction is stuck despite PWL inclusion, escalate BDO -> Project Director DRDA -> PMAY-G helpline 1800-11-6446 / CPGRAMS / UP CM Helpline 1076.
note: This is the decisive approval: sanction authorises the first installment. Sanction depends on annual state target allocation, so an on-list family may wait for its turn in the priority queue.

action: Receive Installment 1 (~Rs. 30,000) via DBT and begin construction at foundation/plinth stage.
on_reject: Non-credit despite sanction: verify Aadhaar-bank seeding, then escalate via AwaasSoft grievance module / helpline.
note: Plain-area UP unit assistance is Rs. 1.20 lakh total, released in 4 installments (approx 30k/45k/30k/15k) tied to construction stages via DBT to the Aadhaar-linked account. Beneficiary is owner-builder. Installment split figures are indicative and may vary by state order.

action: Verify each construction milestone via geo-tagged AwaasApp photo (lintel, roof-cast) to unlock the next installment.
on_reject: If a completed stage is not verified/photo not uploaded, escalate to BDO then Project Director, DRDA.
note: Installments 2-4 release only after stage verification. Milestone photo upload to AwaasSoft is the trigger; delays here are the most common practical bottleneck.

action: Complete the house; claim ~90-95 days MGNREGA wage labour and Rs. 12,000 SBM-G toilet grant via convergence.
on_reject: MGNREGA wage or toilet-grant denial: raise with Panchayat Sachiv/BDO; MGNREGA has its own grievance and social-audit channel.
note: Convergence: 90 unskilled MGNREGA person-days (95 in hilly areas) to the household head for self-construction, paid separately at state wage; SBM-G toilet grant Rs. 12,000 by separate DBT on completion. Person-day/rupee figures per MoRD convergence norms.

post_name: Project Director, DRDA / CPGRAMS / UP CM Helpline (1076)
action: Escalate any stalled stage (no name on PWL, sanction delay, unpaid installment) up the grievance ladder.
note: Ladder: Panchayat Sachiv -> BDO -> Project Director DRDA -> State RD. Cross-cutting: AwaasSoft grievance module, PMAY-G helpline 1800-11-6446 (8am-8pm Mon-Sat), CPGRAMS (pgportal.gov.in), UP CM Helpline 1076. BPL cardholders may file RTI free under RTI Act 2005 s.6(1) for file-movement/fund-release records.

action: Confirm SC caste certificate, current admission, and family income below Rs 2,50,000/year before applying
note: SC/ST income ceiling is Rs 2,50,000/year; student must be a UP resident enrolled in a recognized post-matric (Class 11 onward, incl. college) course. Outside not-official designation: the citizen, noted as such.

action: Generate mandatory One-Time Registration (OTR) on scholarship.up.gov.in using Aadhaar e-KYC
on_reject: Correct Aadhaar name/DOB mismatch and redo e-KYC; update Aadhaar-linked mobile via NPCI if needed
note: OTR (14-digit ID) is mandatory for fresh and renewal applicants from 2025-26; requires Aadhaar-linked mobile. Portal is UP's Samaj Kalyan (Social Welfare) department channel, not NSP for in-state UP applicants.

action: Seed the student's own bank account to Aadhaar via NPCI for DBT before final submission
on_reject: Re-seed the correct account with the bank/NPCI; a wrong or unseeded account blocks disbursal
note: Disbursal is DBT through PFMS to the student's Aadhaar-seeded account, so NPCI seeding is a hard prerequisite.

action: File the post-matric (Dashmottar) application online within the announced window and upload documents
time_limit: Annual window (~2 weeks); e.g. 2026-27 fresh Class 11-12 window announced 11-25 Aug 2026
on_reject: Portal rejects mismatched marksheet/Aadhaar details; correct and resubmit within the window
note: Documents: SC caste certificate, income certificate, previous marksheet, admission/fee proof, Aadhaar, bank details. Name/DOB must match the High School certificate exactly or the application is rejected.

action: Verify enrollment, attendance and fees online and forward the application to the district
on_reject: If status stays 'Pending at Institute', escalate to the institution's nodal scholarship officer
note: Mandatory gate; unverified applications do not proceed. Status: Verified by Institute. Real designation: institution nodal/scholarship officer (outside the listed post set).

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer (Jila Samaj Kalyan Adhikari)
action: Scrutinize the forwarded application at district level and verify eligibility and documents
on_reject: Objection returned to student/institution for correction; contact the District Welfare Officer to resolve
note: District Social Welfare Officer / District Welfare Officer (DWO) is the district-level verifying authority. Status: Verified by District. Real designation (outside the listed rural/revenue post set).

post_name: Director, Social Welfare (SC Welfare Directorate, Samaj Kalyan Nirdeshalaya)
action: Scrutinize district-verified cases at state level and sanction the scholarship
on_reject: Appeal/representation to the Social Welfare Directorate; NSP/portal technical issues via the grievance module
note: State Social Welfare Directorate under the Secretariat's Social Welfare department is the sanctioning authority (Status: Verified by State -> Approved). This is the decisive approval step.

action: Release maintenance allowance and reimbursed fees by DBT to the student's account
on_reject: Failed credit (account/NPCI error) is flagged for re-seeding and reprocessing
note: Payment processed by DBT through PFMS. Maintenance goes to the student; compulsory-fee reimbursement follows the scheme's fee rules. Status: Payment Processed.

action: If stalled, escalate through institute nodal officer, then DWO, then Directorate, then portal grievance
note: Escalation ladder: (1) institution nodal officer, (2) District Social Welfare Officer, (3) state Social Welfare Directorate, (4) portal/NSP grievance module and Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment grievance.

action: Issue caste (SC/ST/OBC) certificate and family income certificate for the applicant family.
on_reject: Apply to Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) / District Magistrate for review of certificate refusal.
note: Prerequisite documents. Income certificate must be within the scheme ceiling; caste certificate must match the claimed category. Both are Tehsildar/SDM-issued via e-district.

action: Complete One-Time Registration and create login on the correct portal (NSP or state).
on_reject: Correct registration details or reset via portal helpdesk.
note: Uttarakhand: National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) with NSP OTR. Uttar Pradesh: state portal scholarship.up.gov.in registration. Confirm which portal applies for the child's category and class band before proceeding.

action: Fill scholarship form, select scheme, upload caste/income/bonafide/marksheet and bank/Aadhaar details.
on_reject: Re-open draft within the application window and resubmit corrected form/documents.
note: Class band determines the sub-scheme (pre-matric usually classes I-VIII or IX-X depending on scheme). Bank account should be student/guardian Aadhaar-seeded for DBT.

action: Verify enrollment, class and application details; forward (Level-1 institute verification).
on_reject: School returns application to applicant for correction; escalate to District Social Welfare Officer if wrongly held.
note: Mandatory institute-level (L1) gate on NSP; application cannot proceed without school forwarding. School confirms bonafide status and that the student is on rolls.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer (Jila Samaj Kalyan Adhikari) / District Backward Classes Welfare Officer
action: Verify caste/income eligibility and documents at district level (Level-2 verification).
on_reject: Application returned with reason; applicant corrects and resubmits, or represents to the officer/District Magistrate.
note: District welfare office checks scheme eligibility and certificate validity. SC handled by Social Welfare, OBC/EBC by Backward Classes Welfare, ST by Tribal Welfare where a separate directorate exists (varies by state).

post_name: State Directorate of Social Welfare / State Nodal Officer
action: Sanction the scholarship at state level (Level-3 verification) after budget/quota check.
on_reject: State-level rejection is communicated on portal with reason; grievance to State Nodal Officer, then Secretary/Director, Social Welfare.
note: This is the deciding step: the state directorate finalizes sanction against the centrally-sponsored scheme allocation. This is where the request is granted or refused.

post_name: State Directorate of Social Welfare (Treasury / DBT)
action: Release sanctioned amount via Direct Benefit Transfer to the Aadhaar-linked bank account.
on_reject: If DBT fails (account/Aadhaar mismatch), correct bank/Aadhaar seeding and re-trigger payment via portal/PFMS grievance.
note: Disbursement is via DBT/PFMS. Pre-matric covers a maintenance allowance and, per scheme, book/tuition components. Payment failures are usually Aadhaar-seeding issues, not re-sanction.

post_name: State Nodal Officer / Portal Grievance Helpdesk
action: Escalate stalled, wrongly-rejected, or technical cases through the portal grievance module.
on_reject: Written grievance to Secretary/Director, Social Welfare Department; state public-grievance system (e.g. UP Jansunwai / CM Helpline) and central CPGRAMS.
note: First chase the level where it is stuck (school for L1, District Officer for L2). NSP has a state nodal officer and grievance/helpdesk; state portals have equivalents. Uttarakhand helpline 1800-180-4236.

action: Verify seller's title: pull mother deed, khatauni/record of rights, and Encumbrance Certificate before committing.
note: Record of rights in UP is the khatauni (upbhulekh.gov.in); Lekhpal/Patwari maintains it. EC and chain-of-title confirm the seller can convey clear title. Due-diligence, not a statutory step.

action: Draft the sale deed: parties, property schedule, consideration, and terms; agreement-to-sell optional.
note: Agreement to sell is customary/protective, not mandatory for conveyance. The registrable instrument is the sale deed itself. Confirmed: registration of the transfer is compulsory under Registration Act 1908 §17.

action: Compute and pay stamp duty on higher of consideration or circle rate, plus registration fee.
note: UP stamp duty ~7% of market/circle-rate value (rebates for female buyers; only ₹5,000 for blood-relative transfers). Registration fee 1%, capped at ₹30,000. Paid via igrsup.gov.in e-stamp. Percentages are state-notified rates, subject to change.

action: If consideration ≥ ₹50 lakh, deduct 1% TDS and deposit via Form 26QB before registration.
note: TDS obligation is on the buyer under Income-tax Act 1961 §194-IA for transactions of ₹50 lakh or more. PAN of both parties (or Form 60) is required at registration.

post_name: Buyer via IGRSUP online slot booking
action: Book an online appointment/token at the Sub-Registrar of Assurances for the property's jurisdiction.
note: Registration Act 1908 §23 requires presentation within four months of the deed's execution. UP uses igrsup.gov.in for slot booking. Jurisdiction is the Sub-Registrar covering the property's location.

action: Verify identities of buyer, seller, and two witnesses appearing in person; capture biometrics/photos.
on_reject: Appeal to District Registrar (Registration Act §72) if refused
note: Registration Act 1908 §34 requires the executants to appear before the registering officer within the presentation window. Aadhaar/PAN, photos and biometrics of parties and two witnesses are taken. The Sub-Registrar (not the District Collector) is the registering authority.

action: Confirm stamp duty/fee paid, admit execution, and register the sale deed in the record.
on_reject: Appeal to District Registrar / Registrar of the district under Registration Act §72 (except where refusal is on denial of execution)
note: This is the decisive step: registration conveys ownership. Registration Act 1908 §72 gives the appeal against a Sub-Registrar's refusal to the District Registrar. Denial-of-execution refusals go to civil suit under §77 instead.

action: Return the registered original sale deed to the buyer after scanning and indexing.
time_limit: Immediately or within a few days
note: Endorsed/indexed original returned to the buyer. Certified copies remain available from the Sub-Registrar's record thereafter.

action: Send intimation of the registered transfer to the Tehsildar to initiate mutation of the record of rights.
note: UP Revenue Code 2006 §34: on registration of a document creating/extinguishing title to land, the registering authority must send intimation to the Tehsildar in whose jurisdiction the land lies — the statutory bridge from registration to mutation.

action: Under Department of Labour, start new Shops & Establishment Act 1962 registration application; upload documents.
note: Documents: premises photo with name board, owner Aadhaar + PAN, address proof + utility bill, bank proof, employee list, constitution proof.

action: File a dakhil kharij (namantaran) mutation application with the registered deed and prior khatauni.
note: Registration transfers ownership but not the revenue record; the buyer should still apply for mutation (dakhil kharij / namantaran) online at upbhulekh.gov.in or e-District so the record of rights and property-tax records are updated. Distinct from registration.

action: Conduct field verification, issue public notice, and report on the mutation application to the Tehsildar.
time_limit: Within the Tehsildar's overall mutation timeline
note: The Lekhpal (Patwari) performs the ground-level verification and objection-notice step feeding the Tehsildar's order. An objection window allows interested parties to contest before the order is passed.

action: Decide the mutation and update the khatauni/record of rights into the buyer's name.
time_limit: ~30-45 days (undisputed); specific limit notified under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 §3
on_reject: Appeal to Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) / Sub-Divisional Officer under UP Revenue Code 2006 §35; then revision to Commissioner under §210. For service delay, first appeal within 30 days under Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 §6.
note: Tehsildar is the mutation authority under UP Revenue Code 2006 (§34 read with the mutation provisions). This is where the collectorate/revenue side (the stated office class) actually comes in. Undisputed cases run ~30-45 days; contested mutations become a revenue proceeding.

action: If registration refused or mutation delayed/denied, pursue the statutory appeal for that stage.
time_limit: Mutation service appeal within 30 days of rejection/expiry (Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam §6)
on_reject: Registration refusal: District Registrar (Registration Act §72), then civil court. Mutation: SDM (UP Revenue Code §35) → Commissioner revision (§210). Service delay: First Appellate Officer then Second Appellate Authority (Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam §6). Fraud/impersonation: police + civil court.
note: Two separate ladders: the registration-refusal ladder under the Registration Act 1908 and the mutation/revenue ladder under the UP Revenue Code 2006, plus the Janhit Guarantee service-delay ladder. Title/valuation disputes proceed as revenue/civil litigation.

action: Confirm the road-owning authority (Nagar Nigam vs PWD vs development authority vs NHAI) at the ward/engineering counter.
note: Only the road owner can grant a cut; if not Nagar Nigam's road the file routes to that owner (PWD/NHAI). Decides everything downstream.

action: Submit road-cut application with ownership proof, trench site-plan, and connection details to the Engineering/Jalkal section.
note: For a water pipe the request is usually bundled with the water-connection application to the Jalkal Vibhag (UP) / Jal Sansthan (Uttarakhand); for cable/telecom the utility often applies on the citizen's behalf.

action: Inspect the site: cut length/width, road surface (bituminous vs concrete), and feasibility.
note: Near-universal step; surface type drives the restoration cost. Post is the ward/zone Avar Abhiyanta of the engineering wing.

action: Compute road-restoration (reinstatement) charge plus permit fee from measured cut area and surface.
note: Charge is per the Corporation's schedule of rates/bye-laws; exact rates vary by city (low confidence on figures).

action: Applicant pays the restoration deposit and permit fee; challan/receipt generated.
note: Deposit is the core financial gate paid before digging; the Corporation (not the citizen) usually restores the road afterward. Keep the receipt.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Obtain traffic-police NOC if the cut affects a busy or main road.
note: City-specific; required only for high-traffic/arterial roads. Routed through the traffic police station, not the local SHO in every city.

action: Approve and issue the road-cutting permit for small cuts, specifying validity window and restoration condition.
on_reject: Escalate to Executive Engineer; then First Appellate Authority under the Janhit Guarantee / RTS Act.
note: Approving rank scales with cut size: minor cuts cleared by the ward Avar Abhiyanta.

action: Approve and sign the permit for larger or main-road cuts (or counter-sign the JE's approval).
on_reject: Escalate to City Engineer / Municipal Commissioner; then RTPS appellate chain.
note: Adhishasi Abhiyanta is the real designation; City Engineer (Mukhya Nagar Abhiyanta) signs off on the largest cuts. Not among the listed post names — official engineering-wing designation used.

action: Citizen executes the cut and lays pipe/cable within the window, through an approved contractor/licensed plumber; JE verifies.
note: Work often restricted to non-monsoon season and to empanelled contractors; notify the section on completion.

action: Corporation restores the road surface (or verifies contractor restoration) and reconciles/refunds the deposit balance.
note: Some cities let a licensed contractor restore and refund; restoration disputes are common, so retain the deposit receipt.

action: Escalate a stalled or wrongly-rejected application to the Commissioner's grievance cell / First Appellate Authority.
on_reject: Second Appellate Authority under U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand RTS Act 2011 (penalty Rs 500-5000) and the Jansunwai-Samadhan portal.
note: For notified services the RTPS chain (Designated Officer -> First -> Second Appellate Authority) applies; the road-cut permit itself may not be separately scheduled, but a bundled water connection usually is.

action: Issue EWS income certificate (and caste certificate if claimed) via e-district before RTE application
time_limit: e-district service limit, commonly ~15 working days
on_reject: Apply again / appeal to the SDM; District Magistrate is the escalation authority for e-district certificates
note: Prerequisite documents. UP EWS income ceiling for RTE is set by the annual notification (commonly Rs 1 lakh/year). Certificate must precede the RTE application.

action: Publish annual RTE admission schedule, participating-school list, and neighbourhood mapping for the district
time_limit: As per State notification; UP runs multiple rounds (typically 4) per year
note: The Directorate of Basic Education notifies the calendar; the BSA is the district nodal officer who publishes school lists and catchment (ward/gram-panchayat) mapping.

action: Parent registers on rte25.upsdc.gov.in and files one online application selecting neighbourhood schools
on_reject: Reapply in the next round of the same year, or next annual cycle
note: Applicant selects schools within the defined neighbourhood radius; distance/ward is the primary selection weight. Only entry classes (pre-primary/Class 1) are eligible.

action: Conduct computerized lottery and publish school-wise seat allotment on the portal
time_limit: On the schedule's allotment date for the round
on_reject: Non-allotted applicants roll to the next round or reapply next cycle
note: Because demand exceeds seats, allotment is by computerized random draw weighted by neighbourhood; result is a specific allotted school.

action: Verify uploaded documents (age, residence, income, category) against originals for allotted applicants
time_limit: Short verification window after allotment (often ~1 week)
on_reject: Correct/resubmit documents; escalate discrepancy to the BSA
note: Verification is at block/nodal level; the school cannot itself re-screen the child. Screening the child or parent is prohibited under Section 13 RTE Act.

action: Approve verified allotment and issue the admission/allotment letter directing the school to admit
time_limit: On allotment confirmation date of the round
on_reject: Represent to the BSA; escalate to District Magistrate / SCPCR (see step 8)
note: This is the decisive approval: a confirmed free seat under the 25% quota. The allotment letter is the parent's entitlement document.

action: Parent reports to the allotted school with the allotment letter; school admits child free of cost
time_limit: Report by the deadline on the allotment letter or seat lapses to waiting list
on_reject: If school refuses/demands money/screens child, escalate to BSA then DM (step 8)
note: School must admit without fee, capitation, or screening (Section 13). Refusal on grounds of pending State reimbursement is not valid — reimbursement is between school and State.

action: On complaint of refusal/fee/screening, direct the school to comply and enforce the RTE seat
on_reject: Escalate to District Magistrate / District RTE Nodal Officer, then State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (UPSCPCR), then High Court writ
note: Grievance ladder: BSA -> District Magistrate (Collectorate) -> UPSCPCR (statutory, Section 31 RTE Act) -> High Court writ. RTE portal also carries an online grievance module.

action: Identify the public authority (department) that holds the record sought.
note: RTI can only be filed with the public authority holding the record; misdirection is the top cause of delay. Which department holds a given record is a factual lookup, not structural.

action: Write request describing information sought; attach Rs 10 fee; no reason required.
note: Section 6 RTI Act: request in writing in English, Hindi, or the official language of the area; no reason or form mandated. Fee Rs 10 per UP/Uttarakhand RTI Rules; BPL applicants exempt on proof (Section 7(5)). Payment mode (IPO/DD/court fee stamp/online) is state-specific.

action: Receive and forward the application to the PIO where filed at sub-office.
note: Section 5(2) RTI Act: APIO (common at sub-district level, tehsil, and post offices) only receives and forwards; adds 5 days to the disposal clock (proviso to Section 7(1)). Skip this step if filed directly with the PIO or via the state online portal.

action: Register application; if misdirected, transfer to the correct authority.
note: Section 6(3) RTI Act: PIO transfers a misdirected application (or the relevant part) to the correct public authority within 5 days and informs the applicant.

action: Notify affected third party where record involves third-party information.
time_limit: 5 days to notify; third party 10 days to object
note: Section 11 RTI Act: PIO gives third party written notice within 5 days; third party has 10 days to represent. Total disposal in such cases extends to 40 days. Applies only when third-party info is implicated.

action: Gather the information and furnish it, or refuse with reasons.
time_limit: 30 days (35 via APIO; 48 hours if life/liberty; 40 with third party)
on_reject: First appeal to the First Appellate Authority under Section 19(1)
note: Section 7 RTI Act: disposal within 30 days of receipt (35 if via APIO). Life/liberty cases: 48 hours (Section 7(1) proviso). Failure to respond in time = deemed refusal (Section 7(2)); no additional fee then chargeable. Refusals must cite exempt provisions (Sections 8/9) and state appeal rights.

action: Hear first appeal on no reply, unsatisfactory reply, or refusal; decide.
time_limit: File within 30 days; FAA decides in 30 days (extendable to 45)
on_reject: Second appeal to the State Information Commission under Section 19(3)
note: Section 19(1) RTI Act: FAA is an officer senior in rank to the PIO within the same department. Applicant files within 30 days of the deadline or response (condonable for cause). FAA decides within 30 days, extendable to 45 with reasons (Section 19(6)).

action: Hear second appeal; order disclosure and impose penalty on defaulting PIO.
time_limit: File within 90 days of FAA decision
on_reject: Writ petition to the High Court under Article 226 (no civil suit; Section 23 bars courts)
note: Section 19(3) RTI Act: second appeal to the State Information Commission (UP: UP State Information Commission; Uttarakhand: Uttarakhand Information Commission). Central bodies go to the CIC instead. Final adjudicator; can order disclosure and impose penalty of Rs 250/day up to Rs 25,000 on the PIO (Section 20). Burden of justifying denial is on the PIO (Section 19(5)).

post_name: Circle Officer / Assistant Commissioner of Police (CO/ACP)
action: On delay or dispute, escalate with the reference number to the sub-divisional police officer.
note: First escalation tier above the police station (CO in districts / ACP in commissionerates).

action: Register the complaint on e-NagarSewa UP portal/app or the ULB helpline; note the complaint number.
note: Portal: e-nagarsewaup.gov.in ('Apply Public Grievance'). Ticket number is your proof and escalation lever. Route garbage to Sanitation/Health wing, drain to Engineering wing. Uttarakhand equivalent: file via Nagar Nigam / serviceonline.gov.in/uttarakhand.

action: Receive and verify the garbage complaint; identify the ward and collection gap.
note: Ward-level sanitation official under the Nagar Swasthya Adhikari (City Health Officer). Field-level dispatch; no senior sign-off for routine lifting.

action: Inspect the overflowing drain; confirm stormwater-drain vs sewer jurisdiction.
note: Corporation Engineering wing handles stormwater/nala de-silting; a separate Jal Sansthan/sewerage board may handle trunk sewers in some cities.

action: Assign crews: safai gang lifts garbage, de-silting gang clears the drain.
on_reject: If not resolved in the charter window, escalate (first appeal) to the Zonal Officer.
note: Stage-1 owner in the e-NagarSewa escalation matrix. Charter SLAs: 24 hrs drain/road cleaning, 1 day garbage pickup/disposal.

action: Flag persistent non-collection politically to push the department.
note: Elected representative; parallel political lever, not a statutory approver. Optional but effective.

action: Re-open the unresolved ticket as first appeal; direct field action.
on_reject: If still unresolved, escalate to City Health Officer / Additional Municipal Commissioner.
note: Stage-2 authority in the e-NagarSewa three-stage escalation.

post_name: Nagar Swasthya Adhikari (City Health Officer) / Additional Municipal Commissioner (Apar Nagar Ayukt)
action: Take up the final internal appeal; order compliance and fix accountability.
on_reject: If unresolved, escalate to the Municipal Commissioner / public grievance cell.
note: Stage-3 authority in the e-NagarSewa escalation matrix.

action: Direct resolution through the corporation's public grievance cell.
on_reject: If still unresolved, escalate to the state portal (Jansunwai / Samadhan).
note: Administrative head of the Nagar Nigam. In smaller towns the counterpart is the Adhishasi Adhikari (Executive Officer) of the Nagar Palika/Panchayat.

post_name: Jansunwai (Samadhan) / Directorate of Local Bodies, UP
action: Lodge a state-level grievance escalating the unresolved municipal complaint.
note: jansunwai.up.nic.in; Directorate of Local Bodies, Lucknow (ph. 0522-2838128/29). Uttarakhand: Chief Minister Helpline 1905 / CM Helpline portal.

post_name: Designated Officer / Appellate Authority under Right-to-Service Act
action: Invoke the statutory time-guarantee if the service is a notified Right-to-Service item.
note: UP Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam 2011 / Uttarakhand Right to Service Act 2011 penalize designated officers for missing notified deadlines. Applies only to services actually notified in each state's schedule; sanitation-specific notification varies by city, so treat as conditional.

action: Submit written TC application to the school Head, giving child's name, class, admission no., destination.
note: Plain written request or the school's TC application form. For RTE-age children the school cannot demand the TC be routed through the receiving school; a direct request to the Head suffices.

post_name: Head Teacher / Principal (Pradhanadhyapak / Prabhari) of the school
action: Receive and acknowledge the application; record it in the school inward register.
