note: The Head is the issuing authority for a routine TC; no higher office is needed for a normal transfer. Ask for a dated acknowledgement.

action: Run no-dues / property check: library books, ID card, any dues (usually nil in free govt schools).
on_reject: Clear the pending item, then re-request; withholding TC for dues cannot delay the child's admission elsewhere (RTE s.5(3)).
note: Government elementary schooling is free (RTE s.3), so dues are typically nil; the no-dues gate is structural, not financial.

action: Prepare the TC from the scholar/admission register: name, DOB, admission & leaving dates, class, conduct.
note: Accuracy depends on the admission register; small schools may have no clerk, in which case the Head fills the form directly.

action: Sign the TC and apply the school seal — the act of issuance; deliver to the parent.
time_limit: RTE-age (Class 1-8): immediately (RTE s.5). Higher classes: ~3-7 working days (administrative norm).
on_reject: If refused/delayed, escalate to the Block Education Officer (Khand Shiksha Adhikari) — step 7.
note: This is the decision that grants the request. For an RTE-age child the Head is statutorily bound to issue it immediately and free; delay is a disciplinary lapse (RTE s.5).

post_name: Block Education Officer (Khand Shiksha Adhikari, BEO) — for inter-district / inter-state moves only
action: Countersign / validate the TC where required for out-of-district or out-of-state transfer.
note: Countersignature is not needed for a local move; it is commonly required only for inter-district/inter-state transfers or for record migration. Real UP designation: Khand Shiksha Adhikari (BEO).

action: Verify the TC against records (may seek confirmation from issuing school), then admit the child.
on_reject: For an RTE-age child, admission cannot be denied/delayed for want of a TC (RTE s.5(3)); insist on provisional admission and file a grievance if refused.
note: RTE s.5(3) bars using absence/delay of a TC to deny or delay a child's admission.

post_name: Block Education Officer (Khand Shiksha Adhikari, BEO)
action: Escalation 1: written complaint; BEO directs the school Head to issue the TC.
on_reject: Escalate to the Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA / District Basic Education Officer) — step 9.
note: First administrative escalation if the Head refuses or delays. In UP the block-level officer is the Khand Shiksha Adhikari.

post_name: Basic Shiksha Adhikari (BSA) / District Basic Education Officer
action: Escalation 2: district-level order directing issuance; can initiate disciplinary action against the Head.
on_reject: File a grievance on the state portal (UP IGRS / CM Helpline 1076; Uttarakhand CM Helpline 1905 / Sewa Ka Adhikar appeal) or approach the Right to Service appellate authority.
note: District head of Basic Education in UP. For secondary schools the parallel office is the District Inspector of Schools (DIOS). Delay in issuing TC is a service lapse actionable here under RTE s.5.

post_name: Right to Service Appellate Authority / State Grievance (IGRS / CM Helpline / RTE grievance officer)
action: Escalation 3: formal grievance/appeal compelling issuance and penalising delay.
note: UP: Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam appellate route / IGRS jansunwai / CM Helpline 1076. Uttarakhand: Right to Service Act, 2011 appellate authority / CM Helpline 1905. RTE grievance also lies with the Block/District Grievance Redressal.

action: Gather establishment, owner, premises and employee details; register on Nivesh Mitra portal.
note: No employee threshold - even a zero-employee proprietor must register. Registering officer of record is the Labour Department, not the municipal corporation (draft's flagged uncertainty confirmed correct).

action: Submit Common Application Form (CAF) on Nivesh Mitra to generate the Unit ID.
note: Single-window: one CAF drives all sub-registrations including the trade-licence requirement.

action: Pay the consolidated registration fee online; fee auto-calculated by employee-count slab.
note: Indicative slabs: ~Rs.40 (no employee), ~Rs.200 (1-5), ~Rs.300 (6-10), ~Rs.500 (11-25), ~Rs.1000 (25+). Exact amount auto-computed on portal.

action: Scrutinise the application and uploaded documents; may route for premises verification.
on_reject: Query/objection raised on Nivesh Mitra; applicant resubmits corrected details.
note: Inspector is a designated officer under the Act (included in the Chief Inspector definition, Sec 29). On the single-window this stage is largely system-driven / near-automatic.

post_name: Inspector / Labour Enforcement Officer, Labour Department
action: Where required, inspect the establishment premises and verify declared particulars.
on_reject: Adverse inspection findings returned as objections; applicant cures and resubmits.
note: Physical inspection is not routine for low-employee shops under the single-window regime; retained as a possible statutory check.

post_name: Chief Inspector (Labour Department), UP Shops & Establishments Act
action: On being satisfied fee is deposited and particulars are in order, register the establishment.
on_reject: Written representation to the Chief Inspector; then appeal to the appellate authority under the Act (Labour Commissioner's office).
note: Statutory registering authority: 'The Chief Inspector shall, on being satisfied that the prescribed fee has been deposited, register the shop or commercial establishment' (India Code / PRS). Includes Deputy Chief Inspector / Inspector.

action: Enter the shop in the statutory register and issue the Registration Certificate.
time_limit: Typically 7-15 working days from valid application
note: Chief Inspector maintains the register of all shops and commercial establishments (Sec 5 read with rules); certificate is issued digitally.

action: Publish the digitally issued certificate for download; applicant displays it at the establishment.
note: Certificate downloadable from Nivesh Mitra. Validity: five financial years; renew before expiry (subsequent renewal up to ten financial years).

post_name: Appellate Authority (Labour Commissioner's office), UP Shops & Establishments Act
action: On rejection or stalled application, hear the applicant's appeal against the Chief Inspector's order.
on_reject: Writ petition to the Allahabad High Court under Article 226 as the ultimate structural remedy.
note: Appeal lies to the designated appellate authority (senior Labour Department officer / Labour Commissioner). Nivesh Mitra also carries a grievance/Jansunwai escalation tracker. Exact appeal window not asserted - verify in the 1963 Rules.

action: Register on state police CCTNS citizen portal, fill Tenant/PG Verification form, upload tenant ID/photo.
note: Landlord (not the tenant) is the applicant. UP: CCTNS citizen portal 'Tenant/PG Verification'. Offline route: submit filled form at the local police station. Post-title is applicant, not an official designation.

post_name: Dealing Assistant / Clerk (Police Station reception / CCTNS operator)
action: Receive request, check completeness of form and attachments, generate acknowledgement/reference number.
on_reject: Incomplete file returned to applicant for missing tenant ID/address proof/photo.
note: Attach: tenant govt photo ID and address proof, tenant photograph, landlord ID/ownership or rent-agreement proof; a registered rent agreement strengthens the file.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Register the verification request at the police station and assign it to the jurisdictional beat officer.
note: The police station with jurisdiction over the property address is the operational host, not the revenue collectorate.

action: Verify tenant identity, address and antecedents; physically confirm occupancy at the property.
note: Beat officer conducts the actual field verification. Real designation: beat/local constable under the SHO.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: If tenant is from another district/state, forward a query to the tenant's home police jurisdiction.
note: Interstate/inter-district tenants require a home-jurisdiction antecedents check, which lengthens processing.

action: Compile findings (clear / adverse antecedents) and submit the verification report to the SHO.
note: Report records whether any adverse criminal record was found.

post_name: Station House Officer / Station Officer (SHO/SO, Inspector)
action: Review the beat report and decide the outcome: no adverse record (clear) or adverse report.
on_reject: Adverse report recorded; landlord may seek review via the Circle Officer/ACP or SP grievance channel.
note: The SHO records the verification outcome. This is the decisive step for the request.

post_name: Superintendent of Police / Commissioner of Police (SP/CP)
action: Final district escalation; also address via state police public-grievance portal or helpline.
note: District SP (or CP in commissionerate cities) heads the police grievance chain. The District Magistrate/collectorate issues the underlying BNSS §163 verification order but does not process individual files.

action: Execute sale; seller endorses/hands over Registration Certificate; both sign Forms 29 and 30.
note: India is single-document: the RC is the ownership record - there is no separate title. Form 29 = seller's notice of transfer; Form 30 = buyer's application. Seller also gives a delivery/sale note.

action: Report the transfer to the registering authority within statutory window to end own liability.
note: MV Act s.50(1)(a): transferor must report within 14 days. Failure keeps seller liable for the vehicle and attracts penalty; keep the dated Form 29 acknowledgement.

action: File Form 30 with RC, insurance, PUC, ID/address proof, sale note, and clearance of dues.
time_limit: 14 days if same registering authority; 45 days if a different one (MV Act s.50(1)(b))
note: Filed on Vahan/Parivahan portal or at the RTO/ARTO. Requires valid insurance in buyer's name, current Pollution-Under-Control (PUC) certificate, and address proof. Late filing attracts penalty per rules.

action: If loan cleared, issue Form 35 to terminate hypothecation; else lender consent required.
note: MV Act s.51 / CMV rule 61: a hypothecated (financed) vehicle needs Form 35 (with No-Objection) to remove the lender's charge before or with transfer, or the transfer records continuing hypothecation.

post_name: Registering Authority (RTO of origin) - Regional Transport Officer / ARTO
action: For inter-state/inter-RTO purchase, issue No-Objection Certificate (Form 28) after dues/theft check.
time_limit: NOC deemed granted if no objection within 30 days (MV Act s.48)
on_reject: Apply to Transport Commissioner if NOC wrongly withheld
note: Only if the vehicle is registered at a different RTO or another state. Form 28 (3 copies) confirms no dues/no criminal record so the vehicle can move to the new jurisdiction. Not needed for same-RTO transfer.

action: Scrutinise Forms 29/30, documents, insurance, PUC, tax and fee payment.
on_reject: Deficiency memo issued for buyer to cure documents
note: Verifies completeness and that transfer fee and any transfer road-tax/re-registration charges are paid. Fees are set by state schedule and vary; verify current amount on Vahan.

action: Inspect vehicle where required (re-registration/inter-state or roadworthiness check).
on_reject: Rectify defects and re-present vehicle
note: Physical inspection is commonly required for re-registration or inter-state transfer to verify chassis/engine number against records; may be waived for routine same-RTO transfers. Official designation: Motor Vehicle Inspector (MVI).

post_name: Registering Authority - Regional Transport Officer / ARTO
action: Record the change of ownership in the register and approve the transfer.
time_limit: As per UP Janhit Guarantee / Uttarakhand Right to Service schedule (commonly 7-30 working days)
on_reject: Written rejection appealable to the State/Deputy Transport Commissioner under MV Act s.50
note: This is the decisive act: MV Act s.50(2) - the registering authority makes the entry of transfer. The RTO/ARTO is a field office of the State Transport Department (secretariat-department class).

post_name: Registering Authority - Regional Transport Officer / ARTO
action: Assign a new registration number and re-register if vehicle moved from another state.
note: Only on inter-state transfer: after NOC (Form 28) the new state assigns a fresh registration mark and levies re-registration road tax (with possible refund of unexpired tax from the origin state). Same-state transfer keeps the existing number.

action: Re-issue the Registration Certificate showing the buyer as registered owner.
note: Updated smart-card RC is issued/dispatched. Buyer should verify ownership on the Vahan portal; seller retains the dated Form 29 acknowledgement as proof of reported sale to defend against future liability.

action: Hear appeal against delay, wrongful rejection, or refusal to transfer.
time_limit: Appeal generally within 30 days of the order
on_reject: Further remedy: State Transport Appellate Tribunal / High Court writ; seller-won't-release-RC is a civil/consumer dispute, not for the RTO
note: Grievance first via Vahan/Parivahan portal or the RTO citing the application reference, then appeal to the Transport Commissioner under MV Act s.50/appeal provisions. A seller refusing to hand over the RC is a contractual dispute for consumer/civil forum.

action: Self-check eligibility: UP resident widow, age 18-60, income below rural 46080 / urban 56460 ceiling.
note: Income ceilings ₹46,080 (rural)/₹56,460 (urban) are widely cited; some recent SSPY notifications state a ₹2 lakh ceiling. No remarriage; not drawing another pension.

post_name: Registrar of Births & Deaths (Municipality / Gram Panchayat via Panchayat Secretary)
action: Register husband's death and issue the death certificate, the core prerequisite document.
time_limit: Certificate issued within notified days once registration is complete (per Registration of Births & Deaths Act, 1969; state RTS schedule).
on_reject: Appeal to the District Registrar (Births & Deaths); invoke U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam appeal if time limit breached.
note: Death within 21 days is free registration; late registration needs an order. This certificate is mandatory and most confident item.

action: Issue income certificate and domicile/residence certificate, applied through e-District / CSC.
time_limit: Income certificate and domicile certificate are notified services under the U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011 (commonly 15 working days).
on_reject: First Appellate Officer (SDM) then Second Appellate Officer under U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011.
note: Lekhpal conducts the field verification feeding the Tehsildar's certificate. Time limits set by the RTS notification schedule.

action: Register on sspy-up.gov.in, fill the Nirashrit Mahila (widow) pension form, upload documents, submit.
on_reject: Correct and resubmit; contact the DPO helpline 1800-419-0001.
note: Documents: husband's death certificate, Aadhaar, domicile, age proof, income certificate/BPL, Aadhaar-linked bank passbook, photo. Print form and submit hard copy to the office within ~1 month.

action: Receive the application, order field verification of widow status, residence and income.
on_reject: Applicant notified; re-verification or correction; escalate to District Probation Officer.
note: Rural applications route through the BDO, urban through the SDM. Grounded in SSPY process pages.

action: Conduct field/physical verification of widowhood, residence and household income; report back.
on_reject: Adverse report can be contested before the SDM/DPO with documentary proof.
note: Village-level verifier; Gram Panchayat / Ward may endorse. Exact title state-specific but Lekhpal is the UP designation.

post_name: District Social Welfare Officer / Women Welfare Officer (block-level review)
action: Scrutinise verified application and forward eligible cases to the district sanction committee.
on_reject: Deficiency memo to applicant; escalate to District Probation Officer.
note: Second-tier scrutiny after field verification, per SSPY four-phase timeline.

post_name: District Probation Officer (DPO) / District-level Sanction Committee under the District Magistrate
action: Approve (sanction) the pension and add the beneficiary to the widow-pension roll.
on_reject: Written reasons issued; represent to DPO, then District Magistrate grievance cell; CPGRAMS; RTS appeal where applicable.
note: In UP the widow pension is run by the Women Welfare Dept (Mahila Kalyan Vibhag); the District Probation Officer is the district nodal officer and the sanction committee sits under the DM/Collector.

post_name: District Probation Officer (DPO) / Treasury via PFMS
action: Release sanctioned pension by DBT to the Aadhaar-linked account; ₹3,000 quarterly.
time_limit: Fund transfer via PFMS ~1 month after sanction; thereafter quarterly.
on_reject: Report non-credit to the DPO / bank; check status on sspy-up.gov.in with registration ID.
note: ₹1,000/month (₹500 state + ₹500 central), paid quarterly as ₹3,000 by DBT/PFMS. Rescinds if beneficiary remarries or income rises.

post_name: District Probation Officer (DPO) grievance cell / District Magistrate (Collector) grievance cell
action: If delayed or rejected, file grievance; track via portal, DPO helpline, or IGRS/CPGRAMS.
on_reject: Escalate to Director, Women Welfare Directorate; then CPGRAMS; ultimately a writ petition to the Allahabad High Court.
note: SSPY helpline 1800-419-0001; UP IGRS (jansunwai.up.nic.in) and CPGRAMS are the standing grievance channels.

post_name: First / Second Appellate Officer under U.P. Janhit Guarantee Adhiniyam, 2011
action: Where the service is RTS-notified, appeal breach of statutory time limit for a directed decision.
time_limit: Appeals decided within the periods fixed by the Adhiniyam (typically 30 days each tier).
on_reject: Second appeal; the appellate authority may impose a penalty (₹250/day up to ₹5,000) on the defaulting designated officer.
note: The RTS route squarely covers the prerequisite certificates (income/domicile) and death registration; whether the pension sanction itself is a notified service varies by the current UP RTS schedule - verify per district notification.
